## P4 - Reboot test passes without verifying the reboot or the watcher ran

**Location:** [tests/16-mikrotik-chr/02-chr-high-ports.robot:51-64](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/tests/16-mikrotik-chr/02-chr-high-ports.robot#L51-L64)

**Problem:** The new test issues `SSHLibrary.Start Command /system reboot` and then asserts that ether64 forwards traffic and that the node is `healthy`, but nothing asserts that the reboot — and therefore the new `watch_reboots` path — actually happened. `RouterOS`&#39;s `/system reboot` normally asks `Reboot, yes? [y/N]:`, and over the non-interactive SSH exec channel that `Start Command` uses the confirmation input may never arrive, aborting the reboot; the same vacuous pass occurs if the command fails for any other reason.

**Trigger:** The reboot command is aborted at the confirmation prompt, fails, or never executes&#58; all assertions pass against the pre-reboot state and CI reports green.

**Impact:** CI would certify the new post-reboot reliability behavior without ever exercising the feature path it was added for, giving false confidence in exactly the scenario this PR targets. Whether the confirmation prompt actually blocks the reboot over an exec channel could not be verified from the repository alone.

**Suggested correction:** Make the pass conditional on evidence that the reboot happened and was observed&#58; assert that `docker logs clab-${lab-name}-r1` contains the launcher&#39;s `RouterOS rebooted: checking the data NICs again` line &#40;logged by `after_reboot` at [`chr-launch.sh:762`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh#L762-L762)&#41;, or that `RouterOS` uptime reset via `/system resource print`, after the `Wait Until Keyword Succeeds` block.


## P4 - 10 s RESET dedup window in `watch_reboots` can swallow a second genuine reboot

**Location:** [nodes/mikrotik&#95;chr/chr-launch.sh:781-791](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh#L781-L791)

**Problem:** The dedup check `[ "${_ts:-0}" -gt $((_last + 10)) ]` exists, per the comment, to collapse the two RESETs of a single reboot, which it says are milliseconds apart, but the implemented window is 10 seconds. Two separate reboots issued within 10 seconds of each other collapse into one post-reboot NIC check, so the second reboot is never re-checked.

**Trigger:** An admin or lab script re-issues `/system reboot` within 10 seconds of a previous reboot.

**Impact:** If a data NIC is rejected only on the second boot, the node keeps reporting `healthy` with a missing data NIC until the next reboot, defeating the feature&#39;s purpose for that `case`.

**Suggested correction:** Narrow the window to something clearly larger than the millisecond double-reset but smaller than a human re-issuing a reboot &#40;for example 2 s&#41;, or keep the current value and add a `ponytail:` comment acknowledging that a reboot within 10 s of the previous one goes unchecked.


## P4 - `after_reboot` keeps the `ready` marker when `RouterOS` never answers after a reboot

**Location:** [nodes/mikrotik&#95;chr/chr-launch.sh:761-780](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh#L761-L780)

**Problem:** If REST does not answer within `$BOOT_WAIT` after a reboot, `after_reboot` logs `data NICs not checked` and returns without touching `READY_FILE`, so the healthcheck keeps reporting `healthy` for a router that is down. This matches the documented design in the section comment and is not a regression over base &#40;which had no post-reboot monitoring&#41;, but the PR introduces the machinery that could close the gap, since the watcher is already waiting on REST.

**Trigger:** `RouterOS` hangs or dies during a guest-initiated reboot and never answers REST again.

**Impact:** The node is dead but reported `healthy` indefinitely, so `wait-for` stages and users relying on the default healthcheck trust a non-functioning router.

**Suggested correction:** Either remove `READY_FILE` in the timeout branch of `after_reboot`, consistent with the launcher&#39;s other FAILED paths that withhold the marker &#40;the default `$BOOT_WAIT` of 300 s makes a merely slow router unlikely to be misreported&#41;, or leave the behavior and document the deliberate limitation in the section comment and the [`mikrotik_chr.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/docs/manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md#L1-L1) paragraph.


## Coverage

- Source-only review&#58; no tests, launcher, or `RouterOS` were executed; conclusions are from inspection of the head and base trees.
- Verified the `check_data_nics` refactor is behavior-preserving against base [`chr-launch.sh`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh#L1-L1) lines 503-534 &#40;stabilization loop, re-plug rounds, `$miss` semantics, failure path `wait`/`exit 0`&#41;.
- Verified both boot paths &#40;first boot line 892, restart line 804&#41; run the boot-time check before `watch_reboots` starts, and that the watcher starts only after `ready` and `mgmt_attach`.
- Verified QMP assumptions from in-repo precedent&#58; `qmp()` already drives the first monitor over busybox `nc`; QMP delivers events only to connected clients, so boot-time RESETs before the watcher connects cause no spurious checks; the event JSON matches the `case` pattern including the space after the colon.
- Verified CI wiring&#58; [`.github/workflows/mikrotik_chr-tests.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/.github/workflows/mikrotik_chr-tests.yml#L1-L1) already selects `01*.robot` and `02*.robot`, so the new test runs without workflow changes; `Login via SSH with username and password` exists in [`tests/ssh.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/tests/ssh.robot#L1-L1).
- Docs &#40;[`mikrotik_chr.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/docs/manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md#L1-L1) line 84&#41; and the launcher header log-line list were updated consistently; no stale references remain. No schema relevance&#58; the changes are internal to the launcher script and [`clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) is untouched and unaffected.
- Unresolved uncertainty&#58; `RouterOS` `/system reboot` confirmation behavior over a non-interactive SSH exec channel, flagged in the test finding; not verifiable from the repository.
- The re-plug gating on `PCI_BRIDGES = 1` &#40;arm64 never re-plugs&#41; is pre-existing behavior preserved by the refactor, not changed by this PR.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

128: +        done
129: +        miss="$(missing_nics)"
130: +        _round=$((_round + 1))

154: +# ---- reboots from inside RouterOS -----------------------------------------
155: +# /system reboot restarts RouterOS but not qemu or this container, and RouterOS
156: +# can reject a NIC again on its way up. QEMU reports the reset as a RESET event

159: +# only when a NIC is still missing afterwards.
160: +qmp_events() { # print QEMU's QMP events, one per line, while qemu runs
161: +    # busybox nc exits when its stdin closes: hold it open for qemu's lifetime
162: +    {
163: +        printf '%s\n' '{"execute":"qmp_capabilities"}'
164: +        while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 5; done
165: +    } | nc 127.0.0.1 "$QMP_EVENT_PORT" 2>/dev/null
166: +}
167: +after_reboot() { # wait for RouterOS to answer, then check the data NICs again
168: +    log "RouterOS rebooted: checking the data NICs again"

170: +    _t0=$(date +%s)

172: +        if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then

175: +        fi
176: +        sleep 2
177: +    done

<content>
1: #!/bin/sh
2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud
3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.
4: #
5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +
6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the
7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces
8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):
9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the
10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no
11: # startup config.
12: #
13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done
14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):
15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)
16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's
17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS
18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: management services
19: #      reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only
20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred
21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,
22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container
23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps
24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is
25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,
26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return
27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches
28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)
29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it
30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu
31: #
32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an
33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW
34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never
35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is
36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are
37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu
38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and
39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management
40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.
41: #
42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,
43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.
44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]
45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env
46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the
47: #   official image's own variables:
48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),
49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)
50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container
51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no
52: #   address on the management network.
53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default
54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.
55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed "chr-launch:":
56: #   "RouterOS ready"                   login + startup config done
57: #   "startup config import FAILED: …"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's
58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)
59: #   "credential bootstrap FAILED: …"   the user/password step failed
60: #   "management setup FAILED: …"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed
61: #   "data NIC check FAILED: …"         RouterOS lacks an interface for a data NIC
62: #                                      even after re-plugging it (also checked
63: #                                      after a reboot from inside RouterOS)
64: #
65: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
66: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
67: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
68: 
69: set -u
70: 
71: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting
72: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.
73: USERNAME="${USERNAME:-admin}"
74: PASSWORD="${PASSWORD-admin}"
75: HOSTNAME_ARG=""
76: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
77:     case "$1" in
78:         --username) USERNAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79:         --password) PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
80:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
81:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;
82:         --trace) shift ;;
83:         *) shift ;;
84:     esac
85: done
86: [ -n "$HOSTNAME_ARG" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG="$(hostname)"
87: 
88: CPUS="${CPUS:-1}"
89: DISK="${DISK:-128M}"
90: INTF_WAIT="${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}"
91: BOOT_WAIT="${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}"
92: INTFS="${CLAB_INTFS:-0}"
93: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc
94: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the
95: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).
96: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped
97: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready
98: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id
99: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics
100: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt
101: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each
102: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out
103: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt
104: MGMT_BR=br0
105: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network
106: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare
107: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt
108: SYSNET=/sys/class/net
109: 
110: log() { echo "chr-launch: $*"; }
111: rm -f "$READY_FILE"
112: 
113: FETCH_PORT=8080
114: # QEMU's QMP monitors, inside the container only: one re-plugs NICs RouterOS
115: # rejected at boot, the other reports guest reboots
116: QMP_PORT=5001
117: QMP_EVENT_PORT=5002
118: 
119: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------
120: IMG=""
121: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f "$f" ] && IMG="$f" && break; done
122: if [ -z "$IMG" ]; then
123:     log "no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image"
124:     exit 1
125: fi
126: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.
127: disk_bytes() {
128:     case "$1" in
129:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
130:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
131:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;
132:         *) echo "$1" ;;
133:     esac
134: }
135: want_bytes="$(disk_bytes "$DISK")"
136: cur_bytes="$(stat -c %s "$IMG" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$IMG")"
137: if [ "$cur_bytes" -lt "$want_bytes" ] 2>/dev/null; then
138:     truncate -s "$DISK" "$IMG"
139: fi
140: 
141: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------
142: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here
143: count_intfs() { ls -d "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }
144: waited=0
145: while [ "$(count_intfs)" -lt "$INTFS" ] && [ "$waited" -lt "$INTF_WAIT" ]; do
146:     sleep 1
147:     waited=$((waited + 1))
148: done
149: log "interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s"
150: 
151: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------
152: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.
153: case "$(uname -m)" in
154:     aarch64|arm64)
155:         QEMU="qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd"
156:         PCI_BRIDGES=0
157:         TCG_CPU="-cpu cortex-a57" ;;
158:     *)
159:         QEMU="qemu-system-x86_64"
160:         PCI_BRIDGES=1
161:         TCG_CPU="" ;;
162: esac
163: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
164:     ACCEL="-cpu host -accel kvm"
165: else
166:     ACCEL="$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on"
167:     log "no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)"
168: fi
169: 
170: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per
171: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the
172: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on
173: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST
174: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).
175: node_id="$(cat "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
176: case "$node_id" in
177:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;
178:     *)
179:         e="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/address" 2>/dev/null)"
180:         if [ -n "$e" ]; then
181:             o2="${e##*:}"; rest_mac="${e%:*}"; o1="${rest_mac##*:}"
182:             node_id="$o1:$o2"
183:         else
184:             node_id="$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 "%02x:"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')"
185:         fi
186:         printf '%s\n' "$node_id" > "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
187:             || log "node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs"
188:         ;;
189: esac
190: NET="-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00"
191: nic_mac() { # nic_mac <index>: the data NIC's MAC, its index in the last octet
192:     printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' "$node_id" "$1"
193: }
194: 
195: check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout
196:     # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. More run into the guest's interrupt
197:     # vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS's PCI I/O space (8 bridges).
198:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 63 ]; then
199:         log "at most 63 data NICs are supported (eth63 / ether64); index $1 is beyond the tested limit"
200:         return 1
201:     fi
202:     # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.
203:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" != 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 29 ]; then
204:         log "at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk"
205:         return 1
206:     fi
207: }
208: 
209: data_nic_device() { # data_nic_device <index> <mac>: the NIC's -device value (also used to re-plug it)
210:     case "$PCI_BRIDGES" in
211:         1)
212:             # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.
213:             # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.
214:             # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.
215:             # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.
216:             # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one
217:             # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.
218:             # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.
219:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 )),addr=$(printf '0x%x' $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))),romfile=,vectors=2"
220:             ;;
221:         *)
222:             # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.
223:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2"
224:             ;;
225:     esac
226: }
227: 
228: qemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments
229:     # Each bridge comes right before its first NIC.
230:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 )) -eq 0 ]; then
231:         _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))
232:         printf '%s ' "-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0"
233:     fi
234:     printf '%s' "-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device $(data_nic_device "$1" "$2")"
235: }
236: 
237: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----
238: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix
239:     ip -"$1" addr show dev "$2" 2>/dev/null \
240:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\{0,1\} \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
241: }
242: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway
243:     ip -"$1" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
244: }
245: M4="$(ip_global 4 eth0)"; M6="$(ip_global 6 eth0)"
246: G4="$(ip_gw 4)"; G6="$(ip_gw 6)"
247: if [ -n "$M4$M6" ]; then
248:     printf 'M4=%s\nM6=%s\nG4=%s\nG6=%s\n' "$M4" "$M6" "$G4" "$G6" > "$MGMT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
249: elif [ -f "$MGMT_FILE" ]; then
250:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments
251:     . "$MGMT_FILE"
252: fi
253: log "management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}"
254: 
255: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap
256: if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR" ]; then
257:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
258:     ip addr flush dev eth0
259:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the
260:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.
261:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null
262:     brctl addbr "$MGMT_BR"
263:     brctl setfd "$MGMT_BR" 0 2>/dev/null
264:     echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
265:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" address "52:54:01:$node_id:00"
266:     ip link set tap0 mtu "$_mtu"
267:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" mtu "$_mtu"
268:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until
269:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's
270:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.
271:     brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" tap0
272:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \
273:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0" "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0" \
274:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0" 2>/dev/null
275: fi
276: ip link set tap0 up
277: ip link set "$MGMT_BR" up
278: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it
279: VM_LL="fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00"
280: VM_EP="$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR"
281: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read
282: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and
283: # the address stays tentative.
284: LL=""
285: bridge_ll() {
286:     _w=0
287:     while [ -z "$LL" ] && [ "$_w" -lt 20 ]; do
288:         LL="$(ip -6 addr show dev "$MGMT_BR" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \
289:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \(fe80::[^/]*\)\/64 .*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
290:         [ -n "$LL" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }
291:     done
292:     [ -n "$LL" ] || log "no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR"
293: }
294: 
295: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
296: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
297: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
298: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
299: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
300: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
301: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
302: max=0
303: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
304:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
305:     n="${d##*/eth}"
306:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
307: done
308: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
309: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
310: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
311: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
312: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
313: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
314: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
315: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
316: check_nic_index "$max" || exit 1
317: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
318: 
319: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
320: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
321: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
322: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
323:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
324: fi
325: 
326: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)
327:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
328:     if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]; then
329:         brctl addbr "br$1"
330:         ip link set "br$1" mtu "$_mtu"
331:         ip link set "tap$1" mtu "$_mtu"
332:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge
333:         echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
334:         brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"
335:     fi
336:     brctl addif "br$1" "eth$1"
337:     ip link set "eth$1" up
338:     ip link set "br$1" up
339: }
340: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link
341: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's
342: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS
343: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.
344: watch_links() {
345:     _warned=""
346:     while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
347:         i=1
348:         while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
349:             if [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i" ]; then
350:                 bridge_eth "$i" && log "link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i"
351:             fi
352:             i=$((i + 1))
353:         done
354:         for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
355:             [ -e "$d" ] || continue
356:             n="${d##*/eth}"
357:             [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] || continue
358:             case " $_warned " in *" $n "*) continue ;; esac
359:             _warned="$_warned $n"
360:             log "link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted"
361:         done
362:         sleep 2
363:     done
364: }
365: 
366: i=1
367: while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
368:     tap="tap$i"
369:     tunctl -t "$tap" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev "$tap" mode tap
370:     [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && bridge_eth "$i"
371:     ip link set "$tap" up
372:     NET="$NET $(qemu_data_nic "$i" "$(nic_mac "$i")")"
373:     i=$((i + 1))
374: done
375: 
376: # shellcheck disable=SC2086
377: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \
378:     -qmp "tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait" \
379:     -qmp "tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_EVENT_PORT,server,nowait" \
380:     -m "$MEM" -smp "cpus=$CPUS" \
381:     -drive "file=$IMG,format=raw" \
382:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \
383:     $NET &
384: QEMU_PID=$!
385: trap 'kill "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT
386: log "qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)"
387: watch_links &

389: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
390: json_str() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'; }
391: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]
392:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI
393:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the
394:     # read timeout (default 20s).
395:     _auth="Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
396:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then
397:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
398:             --header "$_auth" --post-data "$3" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
399:     else
400:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "$_auth" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
401:     fi
402: }
403: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts
404: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({"detail":"Script Error: … (line N column M)"}; its
405: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw
406: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,
407: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite
408: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed
409: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.
410: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived
411:     _cl="$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')"
412:     [ -n "$_cl" ] || return 1
413:     grep -q -m1 '^\r*$' "$1" 2>/dev/null || return 1
414:     [ "$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$1" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$_cl" ]
415: }
416: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> "<status> <body>"
417:     _f="/tmp/chr-rest.$$"; rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"; mkfifo "$_f" || return 1
418:     timeout "$(( $4 + 5 ))" nc "$VM_EP" 80 <"$_f" >"$_f.out" 2>/dev/null &
419:     _pid=$!
420:     exec 7>"$_f"
421:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: [%s]\r\nAuthorization: Basic %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n%s' \
422:         "$2" "$VM_LL" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
423:         "$(printf '%s' "$3" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" "$3" >&7
424:     _left=$4
425:     while kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete "$_f.out" && [ "$_left" -gt 0 ]; do
426:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))
427:     done
428:     exec 7>&-
429:     wait "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
430:     _st="$(head -n1 "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)"
431:     _body="$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')"
432:     rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"
433:     printf '%s %s' "${_st:-000}" "$_body"
434: }
435: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a
436: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently
437: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.
438: is_err() { case "$1" in *'"error"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
439: 
440: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------
441: waited=0
442: AUTH=""
443: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank
444: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username
445: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that
446: # answers is the requested user.
447: while [ -z "$AUTH" ]; do
448:     for _cred in "admin:" "admin:$PASSWORD" "$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"; do
449:         rest "$_cred" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH="$_cred"; break; }
450:     done
451:     [ -n "$AUTH" ] && break
452:     if ! kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
453:         log "qemu exited during boot"
454:         exit 1
455:     fi
456:     sleep 2
457:     waited=$((waited + 2))
458:     if [ "$waited" -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
459:         log "RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running"
460:         wait "$QEMU_PID"
461:         exit 1
462:     fi
463: done
464: log "RouterOS answered after ${waited}s"
465: 
466: # ---- data NICs: every one must be a RouterOS interface ----------------------
467: # RouterOS's kernel can veto a virtio NIC that registers while RouterOS itself
468: # starts up: the driver's probe fails with -1 and the interface never appears.
469: # With more than about 33 NICs one or more are hit, and which one depends on
470: # timing. The NIC itself is fine: plugged in again after boot it registers
471: # normally, and RouterOS re-attaches the port's config, which it keys by MAC.
472: # So wait until the interface list stops growing, then re-plug every NIC
473: # RouterOS lacks, at the same PCI address. The same happens on every boot of
474: # RouterOS, so this runs again after a reboot from inside RouterOS (below).
475: ros_macs() { # the orig-mac-address of every RouterOS ethernet interface, lower case
476:     rest "$AUTH" interface/ethernet | tr '{' '\n' \
477:         | sed -n 's/.*"orig-mac-address":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f'
478: }
479: missing_nics() { # indices of the data NICs RouterOS has no interface for
480:     _have="$(ros_macs)"
481:     _i=1
482:     while [ "$_i" -le "$max" ]; do
483:         case "$_have" in *"$(nic_mac "$_i")"*) ;; *) printf '%s ' "$_i" ;; esac
484:         _i=$((_i + 1))
485:     done
486: }
487: ether_names() { # ether_names <index>...: the RouterOS names of data NICs
488:     for _i; do printf 'ether%s ' $((_i + 1)); done
489: }
490: qmp() { # qmp <command>...: run QMP commands (one JSON object each), print the replies
491:     { printf '%s\n' '{"execute":"qmp_capabilities"}' "$@"; sleep 1; } \
492:         | timeout 5 nc 127.0.0.1 "$QMP_PORT" 2>/dev/null
493: }
494: replug_nic() { # replug_nic <index>: unplug data NIC <index>, plug it back at the same address
495:     qmp "{\"execute\":\"device_del\",\"arguments\":{\"id\":\"nic$1\"}}" >/dev/null
496:     # The guest ejects the device over ACPI hotplug; its id is free once it is gone.
497:     _w=0
498:     while qmp "{\"execute\":\"qom-get\",\"arguments\":{\"path\":\"/machine/peripheral/nic$1\",\"property\":\"type\"}}" \
499:         | grep -q '"return": *"'; do
500:         [ "$_w" -ge 20 ] && return 1

The router IS the node's management address: management services\n19: #      reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n31: #\n32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n35: # binds. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n41: #\n42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); the container itself has no\n52: #   address on the management network.\n53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n56: #   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n57: #   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)\n59: #   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n60: #   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed\n61: #   \"data NIC check FAILED: …\"         RouterOS lacks an interface for a data NIC\n62: #                                      even after re-plugging it (also checked\n63: #                                      after a reboot from inside RouterOS)\n64: #\n65: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n66: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n67: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n68: \n69: set -u\n70: \n71: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n72: # limits on the password); The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n171: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n172: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n173: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n174: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\n175: node_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n176: case \"$node_id\" in\n177:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n178:     *)\n179:         e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n180:         if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n181:             o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n182:             node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n183:         else\n184:             node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n185:         fi\n186:         printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n187:             || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n188:         ;;\n189: esac\n190: NET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\n191: nic_mac() { # nic_mac <index>: the data NIC's MAC, its index in the last octet\n192:     printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$1\"\n193: }\n194: \n195: check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout\n196:     # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. Read\n282: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n283: # the address stays tentative.\n284: LL=\"\"\n285: bridge_ll() {\n286:     _w=0\n287:     while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n288:         LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n289:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n290:         [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n291:     done\n292:     [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n293: }\n294: \n295: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. The count\n298: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n299: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n300: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n301: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\n302: max=0\n303: for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n304:     [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n305:     n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n306:     [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\n307: done\n308: prev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n309: case \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n310: [ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n311: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n312: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n313: # the watcher bridges the late veths.\n314: case \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n315: [ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\n316: check_nic_index \"$max\" || exit 1\n317: [ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n318: \n319: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n320: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n321: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\n322: if [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n323:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\n324: fi\n325: \n326: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n327:     _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n328:     if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n329:         brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n330:         ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n331:         ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n332:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n333:         echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n334:         brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n335:     fi\n336:     brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n337:     ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n338:     ip link set \"br$1\" up\n339: }\n340: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n341: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n342: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n343: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\n344: watch_links() {\n345:     _warned=\"\"\n346:     while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n347:         i=1\n348:         while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n349:             if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n350:                 bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n351:             fi\n352:             i=$((i + 1))\n353:         done\n354:         for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n355:             [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n356:             n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n357:             [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n358:             case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n359:             _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n360:             log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n361:         done\n362:         sleep 2\n363:     done\n364: }\n365: \n366: i=1\n367: while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n368:     tap=\"tap$i\"\n369:     tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n370:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n371:     ip link set \"$tap\" up\n372:     NET=\"$NET $(qemu_data_nic \"$i\" \"$(nic_mac \"$i\")\")\"\n373:     i=$((i + 1))\n374: done\n375: \n376: # shellcheck disable=SC2086\n377: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n378:     -qmp \"tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait\" \\\n379:     -qmp \"tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_EVENT_PORT,server,nowait\" \\\n380:     -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n381:     -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n382:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n383:     $NET &\n384: QEMU_PID=$!\n385: trap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\n386: log \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\n387: watch_links &\n388: \n389: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\n390: json_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\n391: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n392:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n393:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n394:     # read timeout (default 20s).\n395:     _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n396:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n397:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n398:             --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n399:     else\n400:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n401:     fi\n402: }\n403: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n404: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n405: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw\n406: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,\n407: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite\n408: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed\n409: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.\n410: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived\n411:     _cl=\"$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')\"\n412:     [ -n \"$_cl\" ] || return 1\n413:     grep -q -m1 '^\\r*$' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null || return 1\n414:     [ \"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$1\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" -ge \"$_cl\" ]\n415: }\n416: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> \"<status> <body>\"\n417:     _f=\"/tmp/chr-rest.$$\"; rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"; mkfifo \"$_f\" || return 1\n418:     timeout \"$(( $4 + 5 ))\" nc \"$VM_EP\" 80 <\"$_f\" >\"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null &\n419:     _pid=$!\n420:     exec 7>\"$_f\"\n421:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: [%s]\\r\\nAuthorization: Basic %s\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n%s' \\\n422:         \"$2\" \"$VM_LL\" \"$(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\" \\\n423:         \"$(printf '%s' \"$3\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" \"$3\" >&7\n424:     _left=$4\n425:     while kill -0 \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null && ! On a restart the pair that\n446: # answers is the requested user.\n447: while [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n448:     for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n449:         rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n450:     done\n451:     [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n452:     if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n453:         log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n454:         exit 1\n455:     fi\n456:     sleep 2\n457:     waited=$((waited + 2))\n458:     if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n459:         log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n460:         wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n461:         exit 1\n462:     fi\n463: done\n464: log \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n465: \n466: # ---- data NICs: every one must be a RouterOS interface ----------------------\n467: # RouterOS's kernel can veto a virtio NIC that registers while RouterOS itself\n468: # starts up: the driver's probe fails with -1 and the interface never appears.\n469: # With more than about 33 NICs one or more are hit, and which one depends on\n470: # timing. The NIC itself is fine: plugged in again after boot it registers\n471: # normally, and RouterOS re-attaches the port's config, which it keys by MAC.\n472: # So wait until the interface list stops growing, then re-plug every NIC\n473: # RouterOS lacks, at the same PCI address.         "text": "#!/bin/sh\n# chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n# Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n#\n# The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n# /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the\n# node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces\n# the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n# it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n# management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n# startup config.\n#\n# What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n# with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n#   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n#   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n#      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n#      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: management services\n#      reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n#      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n#   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n#      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n#      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n#   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n#      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n#      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n#      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n#      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n#      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n#   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n#\n# Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n# ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n# device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n# binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is\n# recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are\n# persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu\n# carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and\n# their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n# step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n#\n# Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n#   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n# Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n#   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n# Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n#   official image's own variables:\n#   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n#   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n# Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n#   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n#   address on the management network.\n# Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n#   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n# Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n#   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n#   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n#                                      own reason, with the line number)\n#   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n#   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed\n#   \"data NIC check FAILED: …\"         RouterOS lacks an interface for a data NIC\n#                                      even after re-plugging it (also checked\n#                                      after a reboot from inside RouterOS)\n#\n# Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\nset -u\n\n# Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n# limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\nUSERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\nPASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\nHOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n        --trace) shift ;;\n        *) shift ;;\n    esac\ndone\n[ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n\nCPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\nDISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\nINTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\nBOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\nINTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\nSTARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n# Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n# container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\nDONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\nREADY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\nID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\nNICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\nMGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n# every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n# boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\nMGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\nMGMT_BR=br0\n# eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n# namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\nMGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\nSYSNET=/sys/class/net\n\nlog() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\nrm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n\nFETCH_PORT=8080\n# QEMU's QMP monitors, inside the container only: one re-plugs NICs RouterOS\n# rejected at boot, the other reports guest reboots\nQMP_PORT=5001\nQMP_EVENT_PORT=5002\n\n# ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\nIMG=\"\"\nfor f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\nif [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n    log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n# Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\ndisk_bytes() {\n    case \"$1\" in\n        *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n        *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n    esac\n}\nwant_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\ncur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\nif [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; then\n    truncate -s \"$DISK\" \"$IMG\"\nfi\n\n# ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------\n# shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here\ncount_intfs() { ls -d \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }\nwaited=0\nwhile [ \"$(count_intfs)\" -lt \"$INTFS\" ] && [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$INTF_WAIT\" ]; do\n    sleep 1\n    waited=$((waited + 1))\ndone\nlog \"interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s\"\n\n# ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------\n# The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.\ncase \"$(uname -m)\" in\n    aarch64|arm64)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd\"\n        PCI_BRIDGES=0\n        TCG_CPU=\"-cpu cortex-a57\" ;;\n    *)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-x86_64\"\n        PCI_BRIDGES=1\n        TCG_CPU=\"\" ;;\nesac\nif [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then\n    ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\nelse\n    ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n    log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\nfi\n\n# MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n# node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n# interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n# a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n# boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\nnode_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$node_id\" in\n    [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n    *)\n        e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n        if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n            o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n            node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n        else\n            node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n        fi\n        printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n            || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n        ;;\nesac\nNET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\nnic_mac() { # nic_mac <index>: the data NIC's MAC, its index in the last octet\n    printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$1\"\n}\n\ncheck_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout\n    # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. More run into the guest's interrupt\n    # vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS's PCI I/O space (8 bridges).\n    if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" = 1 ] && [ \"$1\" -gt 63 ]; then\n        log \"at most 63 data NICs are supported (eth63 / ether64); index $1 is beyond the tested limit\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.\n    if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" != 1 ] && [ \"$1\" -gt 29 ]; then\n        log \"at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n}\n\ndata_nic_device() { # data_nic_device <index> <mac>: the NIC's -device value (also used to re-plug it)\n    case \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" in\n        1)\n            # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.\n            # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.\n            # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.\n            # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.\n            # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one\n            # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.\n            # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.\n            printf '%s' \"virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 )),addr=$(printf '0x%x' $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))),romfile=,vectors=2\"\n            ;;\n        *)\n            # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.\n            printf '%s' \"virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2\"\n            ;;\n    esac\n}\n\nqemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments\n    # Each bridge comes right before its first NIC.\n    if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" = 1 ] && [ $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 )) -eq 0 ]; then\n        _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))\n        printf '%s ' \"-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0\"\n    fi\n    printf '%s' \"-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device $(data_nic_device \"$1\" \"$2\")\"\n}\n\n# ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----\nip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix\n    ip -\"$1\" addr show dev \"$2\" 2>/dev/null \\\n        | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\\{0,1\\} \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway\n    ip -\"$1\" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nM4=\"$(ip_global 4 eth0)\"; M6=\"$(ip_global 6 eth0)\"\nG4=\"$(ip_gw 4)\"; G6=\"$(ip_gw 6)\"\nif [ -n \"$M4$M6\" ]; then\n    printf 'M4=%s\\nM6=%s\\nG4=%s\\nG6=%s\\n' \"$M4\" \"$M6\" \"$G4\" \"$G6\" > \"$MGMT_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\nelif [ -f \"$MGMT_FILE\" ]; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments\n    . \"$MGMT_FILE\"\nfi\nlog \"management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}\"\n\ntunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap\nif [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR\" ]; then\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    ip addr flush dev eth0\n    # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the\n    # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null\n    brctl addbr \"$MGMT_BR\"\n    brctl setfd \"$MGMT_BR\" 0 2>/dev/null\n    echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" address \"52:54:01:$node_id:00\"\n    ip link set tap0 mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until\n    # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's\n    # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.\n    brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" tap0\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0\" \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0\" \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0\" 2>/dev/null\nfi\nip link set tap0 up\nip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" up\n# RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it\nVM_LL=\"fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00\"\nVM_EP=\"$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR\"\n# The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read\n# once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n# the address stays tentative.\nLL=\"\"\nbridge_ll() {\n    _w=0\n    while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n        LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n            | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n        [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n}\n\n# NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk\n# eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS\n# numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count\n# never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n# every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n# config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n# back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\nmax=0\nfor d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n    [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n    n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n    [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\ndone\nprev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n# The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n# every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n# the watcher bridges the late veths.\ncase \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\ncheck_nic_index \"$max\" || exit 1\n[ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n\n# RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n# requirements). -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n        brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n        ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n        echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n        brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n    fi\n    brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n    ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n    ip link set \"br$1\" up\n}\n# A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n# right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n# redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n# interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\nwatch_links() {\n    _warned=\"\"\n    while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        i=1\n        while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n            if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n                bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n            fi\n            i=$((i + 1))\n        done\n        for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n            [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n            n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n            [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n            case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n            _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n            log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n        done\n        sleep 2\n    done\n}\n\ni=1\nwhile [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n    tap=\"tap$i\"\n    tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n    [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n    ip link set \"$tap\" up\n    NET=\"$NET $(qemu_data_nic \"$i\" \"$(nic_mac \"$i\")\")\"\n    i=$((i + 1))\ndone\n\n# shellcheck disable=SC2086\n$QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n    -qmp \"tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait\" \\\n    -qmp \"tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_EVENT_PORT,server,nowait\" \\\n    -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n    -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n    -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n    $NET &\nQEMU_PID=$!\ntrap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\nlog \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\nwatch_links &\n\n# ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\njson_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\nrest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n    # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n    # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n    # read timeout (default 20s).\n    _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n    if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n            --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    else\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    fi\n}\n# busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n# its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n# /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw\n# HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,\n# reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite\n# `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed\n# once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.\nresp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived\n    _cl=\"$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')\"\n    [ -n \"$_cl\" ] || return 1\n    grep -q -m1 '^\\r*$' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null || return 1\n    [ \"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$1\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" -ge \"$_cl\" ]\n}\nrest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> \"<status> <body>\"\n    _f=\"/tmp/chr-rest.$$\"; rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"; mkfifo \"$_f\" || return 1\n    timeout \"$(( $4 + 5 ))\" nc \"$VM_EP\" 80 <\"$_f\" >\"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null &\n    _pid=$!\n    exec 7>\"$_f\"\n    printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: [%s]\\r\\nAuthorization: Basic %s\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n%s' \\\n        \"$2\" \"$VM_LL\" \"$(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\" \\\n        \"$(printf '%s' \"$3\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" \"$3\" >&7\n    _left=$4\n    while kill -0 \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete \"$_f.out\" && [ \"$_left\" -gt 0 ]; do\n        sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))\n    done\n    exec 7>&-\n    wait \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null\n    _st=\"$(head -n1 \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)\"\n    _body=\"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r')\"\n    rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"\n    printf '%s %s' \"${_st:-000}\" \"$_body\"\n}\n# RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a\n# bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently\n# failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.\nis_err() { case \"$1\" in *'\"error\"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }\n\n# ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------\nwaited=0\nAUTH=\"\"\n# A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank\n# password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username\n# asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that\n# answers is the requested user.\nwhile [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n    for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n        rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n    if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    sleep 2\n    waited=$((waited + 2))\n    if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n        log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n        wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\ndone\nlog \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n\n# ---- data NICs: every one must be a RouterOS interface ----------------------\n# RouterOS's kernel can veto a virtio NIC that registers while RouterOS itself\n# starts up: the driver's probe fails with -1 and the interface never appears.\n# With more than about 33 NICs one or more are hit, and which one depends on\n# timing. The NIC itself is fine: plugged in again after boot it registers\n# normally, and RouterOS re-attaches the port's config, which it keys by MAC.\n# So wait until the interface list stops growing, then re-plug every NIC\n# RouterOS lacks, at the same PCI address. The same happens on every boot of\n# RouterOS, so this runs again after a reboot from inside RouterOS (below).\nros_macs() { # the orig-mac-address of every RouterOS ethernet interface, lower case\n    rest \"$AUTH\" interface/ethernet | tr '{' '\\n' \\\n        | sed -n 's/.*\"orig-mac-address\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f'\n}\nmissing_nics() { # indices of the data NICs RouterOS has no interface for\n    _have=\"$(ros_macs)\"\n    _i=1\n    while [ \"$_i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n        case \"$_have\" in *\"$(nic_mac \"$_i\")\"*) ;; *) printf '%s ' \"$_i\" ;; esac\n        _i=$((_i + 1))\n    done\n}\nether_names() { # ether_names <index>...: the RouterOS names of data NICs\n    for _i; do printf 'ether%s ' $((_i + 1)); done\n}\nqmp() { # qmp <command>...: run QMP commands (one JSON object each), print the replies\n    { printf '%s\\n' '{\"execute\":\"qmp_capabilities\"}' \"$@\"; sleep 1; } \\\n        | timeout 5 nc 127.0.0.1 \"$QMP_PORT\" 2>/dev/null\n}\nreplug_nic() { # replug_nic <index>: unplug data NIC <index>, plug it back at the same address\n    qmp \"{\\\"execute\\\":\\\"device_del\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":{\\\"id\\\":\\\"nic$1\\\"}}\" >/dev/null\n    # The guest ejects the device over ACPI hotplug; its id is free once it is gone.\n    _w=0\n    while qmp \"{\\\"execute\\\":\\\"qom-get\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":{\\\"path\\\":\\\"/machine/peripheral/nic$1\\\",\\\"property\\\":\\\"type\\\"}}\" \\\n        | grep -q '\"return\": *\"'; do\n        [ \"$_w\" -ge 20 ] && return 1",
