1: #!/bin/sh
2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud
3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.
4: #
5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +
6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the
7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces
8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):
9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the
10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no
11: # startup config.
12: #
13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done
14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):
15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)
16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's
17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS
18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: management services
19: #      reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only
20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred
21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,
22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container
23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps
24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is
25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,
26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return
27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches
28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)
29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it
30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu
31: #
32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an
33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW
34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never
35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is
36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are
37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu
38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and
39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management
40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.
41: #
42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,
43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.
44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]
45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env
46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the
47: #   official image's own variables:
48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),
49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)
50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container
51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no
52: #   address on the management network.
53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default
54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.
55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed "chr-launch:":
56: #   "RouterOS ready"                   login + startup config done
57: #   "startup config import FAILED: …"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's
58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)
59: #   "credential bootstrap FAILED: …"   the user/password step failed
60: #   "management setup FAILED: …"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed
61: #   "data NIC check FAILED: …"         RouterOS lacks an interface for a data NIC
62: #                                      even after re-plugging it
63: #
64: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
65: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
66: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
67: 
68: set -u
69: 
70: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting
71: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.
72: USERNAME="${USERNAME:-admin}"
73: PASSWORD="${PASSWORD-admin}"
74: HOSTNAME_ARG=""
75: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
76:     case "$1" in
77:         --username) USERNAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
78:         --password) PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
80:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;
81:         --trace) shift ;;
82:         *) shift ;;
83:     esac
84: done
85: [ -n "$HOSTNAME_ARG" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG="$(hostname)"
86: 
87: CPUS="${CPUS:-1}"
88: DISK="${DISK:-128M}"
89: INTF_WAIT="${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}"
90: BOOT_WAIT="${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}"
91: INTFS="${CLAB_INTFS:-0}"
92: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc
93: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the
94: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).
95: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped
96: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready
97: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id
98: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics
99: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt
100: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each
101: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out
102: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt
103: MGMT_BR=br0
104: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network
105: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare
106: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt
107: SYSNET=/sys/class/net
108: 
109: log() { echo "chr-launch: $*"; }
110: rm -f "$READY_FILE"
111: 
112: FETCH_PORT=8080
113: # QEMU's QMP monitor, inside the container only: re-plugs NICs RouterOS rejected at boot
114: QMP_PORT=5001
115: 
116: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------
117: IMG=""
118: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f "$f" ] && IMG="$f" && break; done
119: if [ -z "$IMG" ]; then
120:     log "no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image"
121:     exit 1
122: fi
123: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.
124: disk_bytes() {
125:     case "$1" in
126:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
127:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
128:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;
129:         *) echo "$1" ;;
130:     esac
131: }
132: want_bytes="$(disk_bytes "$DISK")"
133: cur_bytes="$(stat -c %s "$IMG" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$IMG")"
134: if [ "$cur_bytes" -lt "$want_bytes" ] 2>/dev/null; then
135:     truncate -s "$DISK" "$IMG"
136: fi
137: 
138: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------
139: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here
140: count_intfs() { ls -d "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }
141: waited=0
142: while [ "$(count_intfs)" -lt "$INTFS" ] && [ "$waited" -lt "$INTF_WAIT" ]; do
143:     sleep 1
144:     waited=$((waited + 1))
145: done
146: log "interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s"
147: 
148: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------
149: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.
150: case "$(uname -m)" in
151:     aarch64|arm64)
152:         QEMU="qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd"
153:         PCI_BRIDGES=0
154:         TCG_CPU="-cpu cortex-a57" ;;
155:     *)
156:         QEMU="qemu-system-x86_64"
157:         PCI_BRIDGES=1
158:         TCG_CPU="" ;;
159: esac
160: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
161:     ACCEL="-cpu host -accel kvm"
162: else
163:     ACCEL="$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on"
164:     log "no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)"
165: fi
166: 
167: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per
168: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the
169: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on
170: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST
171: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).
172: node_id="$(cat "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
173: case "$node_id" in
174:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;
175:     *)
176:         e="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/address" 2>/dev/null)"
177:         if [ -n "$e" ]; then
178:             o2="${e##*:}"; rest_mac="${e%:*}"; o1="${rest_mac##*:}"
179:             node_id="$o1:$o2"
180:         else
181:             node_id="$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 "%02x:"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')"
182:         fi
183:         printf '%s\n' "$node_id" > "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
184:             || log "node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs"
185:         ;;
186: esac
187: NET="-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00"
188: nic_mac() { # nic_mac <index>: the data NIC's MAC, its index in the last octet
189:     printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' "$node_id" "$1"
190: }
191: 
192: check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout
193:     # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. More run into the guest's interrupt
194:     # vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS's PCI I/O space (8 bridges).
195:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 63 ]; then
196:         log "at most 63 data NICs are supported (eth63 / ether64); index $1 is beyond the tested limit"
197:         return 1
198:     fi
199:     # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.
200:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" != 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 29 ]; then
201:         log "at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk"
202:         return 1
203:     fi
204: }
205: 
206: data_nic_device() { # data_nic_device <index> <mac>: the NIC's -device value (also used to re-plug it)
207:     case "$PCI_BRIDGES" in
208:         1)
209:             # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.
210:             # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.
211:             # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.
212:             # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.
213:             # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one
214:             # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.
215:             # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.
216:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 )),addr=$(printf '0x%x' $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))),romfile=,vectors=2"
217:             ;;
218:         *)
219:             # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.
220:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2"
221:             ;;
222:     esac
223: }
224: 
225: qemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments
226:     # Each bridge comes right before its first NIC.
227:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 )) -eq 0 ]; then
228:         _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))
229:         printf '%s ' "-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0"
230:     fi
231:     printf '%s' "-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device $(data_nic_device "$1" "$2")"
232: }
233: 
234: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----
235: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix
236:     ip -"$1" addr show dev "$2" 2>/dev/null \
237:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\{0,1\} \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
238: }
239: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway
240:     ip -"$1" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
241: }
242: M4="$(ip_global 4 eth0)"; M6="$(ip_global 6 eth0)"
243: G4="$(ip_gw 4)"; G6="$(ip_gw 6)"
244: if [ -n "$M4$M6" ]; then
245:     printf 'M4=%s\nM6=%s\nG4=%s\nG6=%s\n' "$M4" "$M6" "$G4" "$G6" > "$MGMT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
246: elif [ -f "$MGMT_FILE" ]; then
247:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments
248:     . "$MGMT_FILE"
249: fi
250: log "management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}"
251: 
252: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap
253: if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR" ]; then
254:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
255:     ip addr flush dev eth0
256:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the
257:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.
258:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null
259:     brctl addbr "$MGMT_BR"
260:     brctl setfd "$MGMT_BR" 0 2>/dev/null
261:     echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
262:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" address "52:54:01:$node_id:00"
263:     ip link set tap0 mtu "$_mtu"
264:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" mtu "$_mtu"
265:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until
266:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's
267:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.
268:     brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" tap0
269:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \
270:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0" "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0" \
271:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0" 2>/dev/null
272: fi
273: ip link set tap0 up
274: ip link set "$MGMT_BR" up
275: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it
276: VM_LL="fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00"
277: VM_EP="$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR"
278: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read
279: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and
280: # the address stays tentative.
281: LL=""
282: bridge_ll() {
283:     _w=0
284:     while [ -z "$LL" ] && [ "$_w" -lt 20 ]; do
285:         LL="$(ip -6 addr show dev "$MGMT_BR" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \
286:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \(fe80::[^/]*\)\/64 .*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
287:         [ -n "$LL" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }
288:     done
289:     [ -n "$LL" ] || log "no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR"
290: }
291: 
292: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
293: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
294: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
295: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
296: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
297: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
298: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
299: max=0
300: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
301:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
302:     n="${d##*/eth}"
303:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
304: done
305: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
306: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
307: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
308: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
309: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
310: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
311: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
312: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
313: check_nic_index "$max" || exit 1
314: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
315: 
316: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
317: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
318: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
319: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
320:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
321: fi
322: 
323: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)
324:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
325:     if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]; then
326:         brctl addbr "br$1"
327:         ip link set "br$1" mtu "$_mtu"
328:         ip link set "tap$1" mtu "$_mtu"
329:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge
330:         echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
331:         brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"
332:     fi
333:     brctl addif "br$1" "eth$1"
334:     ip link set "eth$1" up
335:     ip link set "br$1" up
336: }
337: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link
338: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's
339: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS
340: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.
341: watch_links() {
342:     _warned=""
343:     while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
344:         i=1
345:         while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
346:             if [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i" ]; then
347:                 bridge_eth "$i" && log "link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i"
348:             fi
349:             i=$((i + 1))
350:         done
351:         for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
352:             [ -e "$d" ] || continue
353:             n="${d##*/eth}"
354:             [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] || continue
355:             case " $_warned " in *" $n "*) continue ;; esac
356:             _warned="$_warned $n"
357:             log "link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted"
358:         done
359:         sleep 2
360:     done
361: }
362: 
363: i=1
364: while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
365:     tap="tap$i"
366:     tunctl -t "$tap" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev "$tap" mode tap
367:     [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && bridge_eth "$i"
368:     ip link set "$tap" up
369:     NET="$NET $(qemu_data_nic "$i" "$(nic_mac "$i")")"
370:     i=$((i + 1))
371: done
372: 
373: # shellcheck disable=SC2086
374: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \
375:     -qmp "tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait" \
376:     -m "$MEM" -smp "cpus=$CPUS" \
377:     -drive "file=$IMG,format=raw" \
378:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \
379:     $NET &
380: QEMU_PID=$!
381: trap 'kill "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT
382: log "qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)"
383: watch_links &
384: 
385: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
386: json_str() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'; }
387: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]
388:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI
389:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the
390:     # read timeout (default 20s).
391:     _auth="Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
392:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then
393:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
394:             --header "$_auth" --post-data "$3" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
395:     else
396:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "$_auth" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
397:     fi
398: }
399: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts
400: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({"detail":"Script Error: … (line N column M)"}; its
401: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw
402: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,
403: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite
404: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed
405: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.
406: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived
407:     _cl="$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')"
408:     [ -n "$_cl" ] || return 1
409:     grep -q -m1 '^\r*$' "$1" 2>/dev/null || return 1
410:     [ "$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$1" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$_cl" ]
411: }
412: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> "<status> <body>"
413:     _f="/tmp/chr-rest.$$"; rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"; mkfifo "$_f" || return 1
414:     timeout "$(( $4 + 5 ))" nc "$VM_EP" 80 <"$_f" >"$_f.out" 2>/dev/null &
415:     _pid=$!
416:     exec 7>"$_f"
417:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: [%s]\r\nAuthorization: Basic %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n%s' \
418:         "$2" "$VM_LL" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
419:         "$(printf '%s' "$3" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" "$3" >&7
420:     _left=$4
421:     while kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete "$_f.out" && [ "$_left" -gt 0 ]; do
422:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))
423:     done
424:     exec 7>&-
425:     wait "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
426:     _st="$(head -n1 "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)"
427:     _body="$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')"
428:     rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"
429:     printf '%s %s' "${_st:-000}" "$_body"
430: }
431: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a
432: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently
433: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.
434: is_err() { case "$1" in *'"error"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
435: 
436: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------
437: waited=0
438: AUTH=""
439: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank
440: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username
441: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that
442: # answers is the requested user.
443: while [ -z "$AUTH" ]; do
444:     for _cred in "admin:" "admin:$PASSWORD" "$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"; do
445:         rest "$_cred" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH="$_cred"; break; }
446:     done
447:     [ -n "$AUTH" ] && break
448:     if ! kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
449:         log "qemu exited during boot"
450:         exit 1
451:     fi
452:     sleep 2
453:     waited=$((waited + 2))
454:     if [ "$waited" -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
455:         log "RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running"
456:         wait "$QEMU_PID"
457:         exit 1
458:     fi
459: done
460: log "RouterOS answered after ${waited}s"
461: 
462: # ---- data NICs: every one must be a RouterOS interface ----------------------
463: # RouterOS's kernel can veto a virtio NIC that registers while RouterOS itself
464: # starts up: the driver's probe fails with -1 and the interface never appears.
465: # With more than about 33 NICs one or more are hit, and which one depends on
466: # timing. The NIC itself is fine: plugged in again after boot it registers
467: # normally, and RouterOS re-attaches the port's config, which it keys by MAC.
468: # So wait until the interface list stops growing, then re-plug every NIC
469: # RouterOS lacks, at the same PCI address.
470: ros_macs() { # the orig-mac-address of every RouterOS ethernet interface, lower case
471:     rest "$AUTH" interface/ethernet | tr '{' '\n' \
472:         | sed -n 's/.*"orig-mac-address":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f'
473: }
474: missing_nics() { # indices of the data NICs RouterOS has no interface for
475:     _have="$(ros_macs)"
476:     _i=1
477:     while [ "$_i" -le "$max" ]; do
478:         case "$_have" in *"$(nic_mac "$_i")"*) ;; *) printf '%s ' "$_i" ;; esac
479:         _i=$((_i + 1))
480:     done
481: }
482: ether_names() { # ether_names <index>...: the RouterOS names of data NICs
483:     for _i; do printf 'ether%s ' $((_i + 1)); done
484: }
485: qmp() { # qmp <command>...: run QMP commands (one JSON object each), print the replies

    "output": "<path>/source/base/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: #!/bin/sh\n2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n4: #\n5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). It replaces\n8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n11: # startup config.\n12: #\n13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: management services\n19: #      reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n31: #\n32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. then\n161:     ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\n162: else\n163:     ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n164:     log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\n165: fi\n166: \n167: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n168: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n169: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). The id is read on the FIRST\n171: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\n172: node_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n173: case \"$node_id\" in\n174:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n175:     *)\n176:         e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n177:         if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n178:             o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n179:             node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n180:         else\n181:             node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n182:         fi\n183:         printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n184:             || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n185:         ;;\n186: esac\n187: NET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\n188: nic_mac() { # nic_mac <index>: the data NIC's MAC, its index in the last octet\n189:     printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$1\"\n190: }\n191: \n192: check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout\n193:     # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n298: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\n299: max=0\n300: for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n301:     [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n302:     n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n303:     [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\n304: done\n305: prev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n306: case \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n307: [ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n308: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n309: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n310: # the watcher bridges the late veths.\n311: case \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n312: [ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\n313: check_nic_index \"$max\" || exit 1\n314: [ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n315: \n316: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n317: # requirements). -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n326:         brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n327:         ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n328:         ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n329:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n330:         echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n331:         brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n332:     fi\n333:     brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n334:     ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n335:     ip link set \"br$1\" up\n336: }\n337: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n338: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n339: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n340: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\n341: watch_links() {\n342:     _warned=\"\"\n343:     while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n344:         i=1\n345:         while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n346:             if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n347:                 bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n348:             fi\n349:             i=$((i + 1))\n350:         done\n351:         for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n352:             [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n353:             n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n354:             [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n355:             case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n356:             _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n357:             log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n358:         done\n359:         sleep 2\n360:     done\n361: }\n362: \n363: i=1\n364: while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n365:     tap=\"tap$i\"\n366:     tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n367:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n368:     ip link set \"$tap\" up\n369:     NET=\"$NET $(qemu_data_nic \"$i\" \"$(nic_mac \"$i\")\")\"\n370:     i=$((i + 1))\n371: done\n372: \n373: # shellcheck disable=SC2086\n374: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n375:     -qmp \"tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait\" \\\n376:     -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n377:     -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n378:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n379:     $NET &\n380: QEMU_PID=$!\n381: trap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\n382: log \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\n383: watch_links &\n384: \n385: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\n386: json_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\n387: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n388:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n389:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n390:     # read timeout (default 20s).\n391:     _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n392:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n393:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n394:             --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n395:     else\n396:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n397:     fi\n398: }\n399: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n400: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n401: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw\n402: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,\n403: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite\n404: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed\n405: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.\n406: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived\n407:     _cl=\"$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')\"\n408:     [ -n \"$_cl\" ] || return 1\n409:     grep -q -m1 '^\\r*$' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null || return 1\n410:     [ \"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$1\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" -ge \"$_cl\" ]\n411: }\n412: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> \"<status> <body>\"\n413:     _f=\"/tmp/chr-rest.$$\"; rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"; mkfifo \"$_f\" || return 1\n414:     timeout \"$(( $4 + 5 ))\" nc \"$VM_EP\" 80 <\"$_f\" >\"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null &\n415:     _pid=$!\n416:     exec 7>\"$_f\"\n417:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: [%s]\\r\\nAuthorization: Basic %s\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n%s' \\\n418:         \"$2\" \"$VM_LL\" \"$(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\" \\\n419:         \"$(printf '%s' \"$3\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" \"$3\" >&7\n420:     _left=$4\n421:     while kill -0 \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete \"$_f.out\" && [ \"$_left\" -gt 0 ]; do\n422:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))\n423:     done\n424:     exec 7>&-\n425:     wait \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null\n426:     _st=\"$(head -n1 \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)\"\n427:     _body=\"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r')\"\n428:     rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"\n429:     printf '%s %s' \"${_st:-000}\" \"$_body\"\n430: }\n431: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a\n432: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently\n433: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.\n434: is_err() { case \"$1\" in *'\"error\"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }\n435: \n436: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------\n437: waited=0\n438: AUTH=\"\"\n439: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank\n440: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username\n441: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that\n442: # answers is the requested user.\n443: while [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n444:     for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n445:         rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n446:     done\n447:     [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n448:     if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n449:         log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n450:         exit 1\n451:     fi\n452:     sleep 2\n453:     waited=$((waited + 2))\n454:     if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n455:         log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n456:         wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n457:         exit 1\n458:     fi\n459: done\n460: log \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n461: \n462: # ---- data NICs: every one must be a RouterOS interface ----------------------\n463: # RouterOS's kernel can veto a virtio NIC that registers while RouterOS itself\n464: # starts up: the driver's probe fails with -1 and the interface never appears.\n465: # With more than about 33 NICs one or more are hit, and which one depends on\n466: # timing. The NIC itself is fine: plugged in again after boot it registers\n467: # normally, and RouterOS re-attaches the port's config, which it keys by MAC.\n468: # So wait until the interface list stops growing, then re-plug every NIC\n469: # RouterOS lacks, at the same PCI address.\n470: ros_macs() { # the orig-mac-address of every RouterOS ethernet interface, lower case\n471:     rest \"$AUTH\" interface/ethernet | tr '{' '\\n' \\\n472:         | sed -n 's/.*\"orig-mac-address\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f'\n473: }\n474: missing_nics() { # indices of the data NICs RouterOS has no interface for\n475:     _have=\"$(ros_macs)\"\n476:     _i=1\n477:     while [ \"$_i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n478:         case \"$_have\" in *\"$(nic_mac \"$_i\")\"*) ;; *) printf '%s ' \"$_i\" ;; esac\n479:         _i=$((_i + 1))\n480:     done\n481: }\n482: ether_names() { # ether_names <index>...: the RouterOS names of data NICs\n483:     for _i; do printf 'ether%s ' $((_i + 1)); done\n484: }\n485: qmp() { # qmp <command>...: run QMP commands (one JSON object each), print the replies\n486:     { printf '%s\\n' '{\"execute\":\"qmp_capabilities\"}' \"$@\"; sleep 1; } \\\n487:         | timeout 5 nc 127.0.0.1 \"$QMP_PORT\" 2>/dev/null\n488: }\n489: replug_nic() { # replug_nic <index>: unplug data NIC <index>, plug it back at the same address\n490:     qmp \"{\\\"execute\\\":\\\"device_del\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":{\\\"id\\\":\\\"nic$1\\\"}}\" >/dev/null\n491:     # The guest ejects the device over ACPI hotplug; its id is free once it is gone.\n492:     _w=0\n493:     while qmp \"{\\\"execute\\\":\\\"qom-get\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":{\\\"path\\\":\\\"/machine/peripheral/nic$1\\\",\\\"property\\\":\\\"type\\\"}}\" \\\n494:         | grep -q '\"return\": *\"'; do\n495:         [ \"$_w\" -ge 20 ] && return 1\n496:         sleep 1\n497:         _w=$((_w + 1))\n498:     done\n499:     # human-monitor-command answers \"\" on success, the error text otherwise\n500:     qmp \"{\\\"execute\\\":\\\"human-monitor-command\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":{\\\"command-line\\\":\\\"device_add $(data_nic_device \"$1\" \"$(nic_mac \"$1\")\")\\\"}}\" \\\n\n(Showing lines 1-500 of 837.         "text": "#!/bin/sh\n# chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n# Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n#\n# The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n# /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the\n# node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces\n# the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n# it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n# management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n# startup config.\n#\n# What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n# with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n#   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n#   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n#      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n#      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: management services\n#      reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n#      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n#   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n#      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n#      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n#   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n#      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n#      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n#      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n#      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n#      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n#   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n#\n# Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n# ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n# device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n# binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is\n# recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are\n# persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu\n# carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and\n# their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n# step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n#\n# Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n#   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n# Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n#   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n# Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n#   official image's own variables:\n#   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n#   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n# Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n#   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n#   address on the management network.\n# Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n#   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n# Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n#   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n#   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n#                                      own reason, with the line number)\n#   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n#   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed\n#   \"data NIC check FAILED: …\"         RouterOS lacks an interface for a data NIC\n#                                      even after re-plugging it\n#\n# Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\nset -u\n\n# Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n# limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\nUSERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\nPASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\nHOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n        --trace) shift ;;\n        *) shift ;;\n    esac\ndone\n[ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n\nCPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\nDISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\nINTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\nBOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\nINTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\nSTARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n# Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n# container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\nDONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\nREADY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\nID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\nNICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\nMGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n# every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n# boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\nMGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\nMGMT_BR=br0\n# eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n# namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\nMGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\nSYSNET=/sys/class/net\n\nlog() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\nrm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n\nFETCH_PORT=8080\n# QEMU's QMP monitor, inside the container only: re-plugs NICs RouterOS rejected at boot\nQMP_PORT=5001\n\n# ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\nIMG=\"\"\nfor f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\nif [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n    log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n# Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\ndisk_bytes() {\n    case \"$1\" in\n        *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n        *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n    esac\n}\nwant_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\ncur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\nif [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; then\n    truncate -s \"$DISK\" \"$IMG\"\nfi\n\n# ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------\n# shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here\ncount_intfs() { ls -d \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }\nwaited=0\nwhile [ \"$(count_intfs)\" -lt \"$INTFS\" ] && [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$INTF_WAIT\" ]; do\n    sleep 1\n    waited=$((waited + 1))\ndone\nlog \"interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s\"\n\n# ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------\n# The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.\ncase \"$(uname -m)\" in\n    aarch64|arm64)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd\"\n        PCI_BRIDGES=0\n        TCG_CPU=\"-cpu cortex-a57\" ;;\n    *)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-x86_64\"\n        PCI_BRIDGES=1\n        TCG_CPU=\"\" ;;\nesac\nif [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then\n    ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\nelse\n    ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n    log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\nfi\n\n# MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n# node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n# interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n# a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n# boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\nnode_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$node_id\" in\n    [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n    *)\n        e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n        if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n            o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n            node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n        else\n            node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n        fi\n        printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n            || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n        ;;\nesac\nNET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\nnic_mac() { # nic_mac <index>: the data NIC's MAC, its index in the last octet\n    printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$1\"\n}\n\ncheck_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout\n    # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. More run into the guest's interrupt\n    # vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS's PCI I/O space (8 bridges).\n    if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" = 1 ] && [ \"$1\" -gt 63 ]; then\n        log \"at most 63 data NICs are supported (eth63 / ether64); index $1 is beyond the tested limit\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.\n    if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" != 1 ] && [ \"$1\" -gt 29 ]; then\n        log \"at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n}\n\ndata_nic_device() { # data_nic_device <index> <mac>: the NIC's -device value (also used to re-plug it)\n    case \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" in\n        1)\n            # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.\n            # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.\n            # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.\n            # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.\n            # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one\n            # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.\n            # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.\n            printf '%s' \"virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 )),addr=$(printf '0x%x' $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))),romfile=,vectors=2\"\n            ;;\n        *)\n            # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.\n            printf '%s' \"virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2\"\n            ;;\n    esac\n}\n\nqemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments\n    # Each bridge comes right before its first NIC.\n    if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" = 1 ] && [ $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 )) -eq 0 ]; then\n        _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))\n        printf '%s ' \"-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0\"\n    fi\n    printf '%s' \"-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device $(data_nic_device \"$1\" \"$2\")\"\n}\n\n# ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----\nip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix\n    ip -\"$1\" addr show dev \"$2\" 2>/dev/null \\\n        | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\\{0,1\\} \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway\n    ip -\"$1\" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nM4=\"$(ip_global 4 eth0)\"; M6=\"$(ip_global 6 eth0)\"\nG4=\"$(ip_gw 4)\"; G6=\"$(ip_gw 6)\"\nif [ -n \"$M4$M6\" ]; then\n    printf 'M4=%s\\nM6=%s\\nG4=%s\\nG6=%s\\n' \"$M4\" \"$M6\" \"$G4\" \"$G6\" > \"$MGMT_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\nelif [ -f \"$MGMT_FILE\" ]; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments\n    . \"$MGMT_FILE\"\nfi\nlog \"management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}\"\n\ntunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap\nif [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR\" ]; then\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    ip addr flush dev eth0\n    # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the\n    # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null\n    brctl addbr \"$MGMT_BR\"\n    brctl setfd \"$MGMT_BR\" 0 2>/dev/null\n    echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" address \"52:54:01:$node_id:00\"\n    ip link set tap0 mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until\n    # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's\n    # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.\n    brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" tap0\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0\" \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0\" \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0\" 2>/dev/null\nfi\nip link set tap0 up\nip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" up\n# RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it\nVM_LL=\"fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00\"\nVM_EP=\"$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR\"\n# The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read\n# once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n# the address stays tentative.\nLL=\"\"\nbridge_ll() {\n    _w=0\n    while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n        LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n            | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n        [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n}\n\n# NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk\n# eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS\n# numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count\n# never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n# every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n# config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n# back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\nmax=0\nfor d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n    [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n    n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n    [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\ndone\nprev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n# The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n# every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n# the watcher bridges the late veths.\ncase \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\ncheck_nic_index \"$max\" || exit 1\n[ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n\n# RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n# requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n# link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\nif [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n    MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\nfi\n\nbridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n        brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n        ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n        echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n        brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n    fi\n    brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n    ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n    ip link set \"br$1\" up\n}\n# A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n# right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n# redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n# interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\nwatch_links() {\n    _warned=\"\"\n    while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        i=1\n        while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n            if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n                bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n            fi\n            i=$((i + 1))\n        done\n        for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n            [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n            n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n            [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n            case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n            _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n            log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n        done\n        sleep 2\n    done\n}\n\ni=1\nwhile [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n    tap=\"tap$i\"\n    tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n    [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n    ip link set \"$tap\" up\n    NET=\"$NET $(qemu_data_nic \"$i\" \"$(nic_mac \"$i\")\")\"\n    i=$((i + 1))\ndone\n\n# shellcheck disable=SC2086\n$QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n    -qmp \"tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait\" \\\n    -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n    -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n    -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n    $NET &\nQEMU_PID=$!\ntrap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\nlog \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\nwatch_links &\n\n# ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\njson_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\nrest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n    # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n    # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n    # read timeout (default 20s).\n    _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n    if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n            --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    else\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    fi\n}\n# busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n# its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n# /log stays silent). On a restart the pair that\n# answers is the requested user.\nwhile [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n    for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n        rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n    if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    sleep 2\n    waited=$((waited + 2))\n    if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n        log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n        wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\ndone\nlog \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n\n# ---- data NICs: every one must be a RouterOS interface ----------------------\n# RouterOS's kernel can veto a virtio NIC that registers while RouterOS itself\n# starts up: the driver's probe fails with -1 and the interface never appears.\n# With more than about 33 NICs one or more are hit, and which one depends on\n# timing. 545: # Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST
546: # answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the
547: # configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.
548: # A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is
549: # logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).
550: ssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc "$VM_EP" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }
551: ready() {
552:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/service?name=ssh")" in
553:         *'"disabled":"false"'*)
554:             _t0=$(date +%s)
555:             until [ "$(ssh_banner)" = "SSH-2.0" ]; do
556:                 if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
557:                     log "SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)"
558:                     break
559:                 fi
560:                 sleep 2
561:             done
562:             ;;
563:     esac
564:     touch "$READY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
565:     log "RouterOS ready"

577: # The VRF owns its routing table and connected routes. Services must bind to

580: mgmt_fail() {

602: }
603: # A native VRF creates its routing table asynchronously. Move the interface
604: # and services together in a router-local background job, then prove the
605: # handoff before configuring addresses/routes or attaching external eth0.
606: mgmt_vrf_ready() {
607:     rest_has "ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false" || return 1
608:     rest_has "routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE&dynamic=true&invalid=false" || return 1
609:     for _svc in ssh www www-ssl api api-ssl winbox telnet; do
610:         rest_has "ip/service?name=$_svc&vrf=$MGMT_TABLE&dynamic=false" || return 1
611:     done
612:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" snmp)" in
613:         *"\"vrf\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\""*) return 0 ;;
614:         *) return 1 ;;
615:     esac
616: }
617: mgmt_vrf() {
618:     if rest_has "ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false"; then
619:         # User service overrides are applied by startup-config, after the
620:         # first-boot defaults. Do not overwrite them on a restart.
621:         [ -f "$DONE_MARKER" ] && return 0
622:     else
623:         if rest_has "routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE"; then
624:             mgmt_fail "table $MGMT_TABLE already exists without the launcher's VRF; use a fresh container"
625:         fi
626:         _script=":delay 1s; /ip vrf add name=$MGMT_TABLE interfaces=ether1 place-before=0 comment=$MGMT_COMMENT; /ip service set ssh,www,www-ssl,api,api-ssl,winbox,telnet vrf=$MGMT_TABLE; /snmp set vrf=$MGMT_TABLE"
627:         rest_add "start management VRF handoff" execute "{\"script\":\"$(json_str "$_script")\"}"
628:     fi
629:     _start=$(date +%s)
630:     until mgmt_vrf_ready; do
631:         [ $(( $(date +%s) - _start )) -lt "$BOOT_WAIT" ] \
632:             || mgmt_fail "VRF handoff did not complete; inspect RouterOS script errors through the serial console"
633:         sleep 1
634:     done
635:     log "management VRF $MGMT_TABLE: ether1, routing table and service bindings verified"
636: }
637: # The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with
638: # the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.
639: mgmt_in_place() {
640:     _want=0
641:     rest_has "ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false" || return 1
642:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
643:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
644:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_has "ip/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=0.0.0.0/0&gateway=$G4@$MGMT_TABLE" || return 1
645:         _want=$((_want + 1))
646:     fi
647:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
648:         rest_has "ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
649:         [ -z "$G6" ] || rest_has "ipv6/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=::/0&gateway=$G6@$MGMT_TABLE" || return 1
650:         _want=$((_want + 1))
651:     fi
652:     [ "$(rest_count "ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")$(rest_count "ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")" \
653:         = "$([ -n "$M4" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n "$M6" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" ] || return 1
654:     rest_has "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none" || return 1
655:     [ "$_want" -gt 0 ]
656: }
657: mgmt_setup() {
658:     mgmt_vrf
659:     if mgmt_in_place; then
660:         log "management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}"
661:         return 0
662:     fi
663:     for _m in ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear "$_m"; done
664:     _c="\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\""
665:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
666:         rest_add "ether1 address $M4" ip/address/add "{\"address\":\"$M4\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",$_c}"
667:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_add "default via $G4 in VRF $MGMT_TABLE" ip/route/add \
668:             "{\"dst-address\":\"0.0.0.0/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G4@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
669:     fi
670:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
671:         rest_add "ether1 address $M6" ipv6/address/add \
672:             "{\"address\":\"$M6\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"advertise\":\"no\",$_c}"
673:         [ -z "$G6" ] || rest_add "IPv6 default via $G6 in VRF $MGMT_TABLE" ipv6/route/add \
674:             "{\"dst-address\":\"::/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G6@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
675:     fi
676:     _id="$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/dhcp-client?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
677:     [ -z "$_id" ] || rest_add "disable the ether1 DHCP client" ip/dhcp-client/set \
678:         "{\"numbers\":\"$_id\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}"
679:     # RouterOS's default ND entry (interface=all, ra-lifetime=30m) sends router
680:     # advertisements on ether1 too, and every host on the management network
681:     # with accept_ra would install the router as its IPv6 default route. An
682:     # ether1 entry with ra-lifetime=none keeps the RAs harmless and withdraws a
683:     # route a host already learned (a disabled entry does not override "all").
684:     # /ipv6/nd keeps no comment, so its entry is found by interface.
685:     _nd="$(rest "$AUTH" "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
686:     if [ -n "$_nd" ]; then
687:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/set \
688:             "{\"numbers\":\"$_nd\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\",\"disabled\":\"no\"}"
689:     else
690:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/add \
691:             "{\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\"}"
692:     fi
693:     # Prove they took (a transport flake answers an empty body, which is not
694:     # an error by the set-contract).
695:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
696:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4" || mgmt_fail "$M4 not on ether1"
697:     fi
698:     mgmt_in_place || mgmt_fail "management addressing or routes not applied"
699:     log "management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in VRF $MGMT_TABLE"
700: }
701: # Keep discovery on static data interfaces, excluding management. Set this only
702: # on first boot, before attaching eth0: startup-config and subsequent user changes
703: # can select a different list, and restarts must preserve that choice.
704: discovery_setup() {
705:     rest_add "management interface list" interface/list/add \
706:         "{\"name\":\"clab-management\",\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\"}"
707:     rest_add "management interface list member" interface/list/member/add \
708:         "{\"list\":\"clab-management\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\"}"
709:     rest_add "discovery interface list" interface/list/add \
710:         "{\"name\":\"clab-discovery\",\"include\":\"static\",\"exclude\":\"clab-management\",\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\"}"
711:     rest_add "management discovery off" ip/neighbor/discovery-settings/set \
712:         '{"discover-interface-list":"clab-discovery"}'
713:     rest_has "interface/list?name=clab-management&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" \
714:         || mgmt_fail "management interface list not applied"
715:     rest_has "interface/list/member?list=clab-management&interface=ether1&disabled=false&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" \
716:         || mgmt_fail "management interface list member not applied"
717:     rest_has "interface/list?name=clab-discovery&include=static&exclude=clab-management&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" \
718:         || mgmt_fail "discovery interface list not applied"
719:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" ip/neighbor/discovery-settings)" in
720:         *'"discover-interface-list":"clab-discovery"'*) : ;;
721:         *) mgmt_fail "management discovery policy not applied" ;;
722:     esac
723:     log "neighbor discovery: static interfaces except ether1 (clab-discovery)"
724: }
725: # Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the
726: # management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request
727: # refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC
728: # before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).
729: mgmt_attach() {
730:     [ -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0" ] || brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" eth0
731:     ip link set eth0 up
732:     for _pair in "$G4 ${M4%/*}" "$G6 ${M6%/*}"; do
733:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # split "gateway source"; an empty half skips the pair
734:         set -- $_pair
735:         [ $# -eq 2 ] || continue
736:         _t0=$(date +%s)
737:         until case "$(rest "$AUTH" ping "{\"address\":\"$1\",\"src-address\":\"$2\",\"count\":\"2\",\"vrf\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\"}")" in
738:                 *'"received":"'[1-9]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; do
739:             if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then
740:                 log "gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)"
741:                 break
742:             fi
743:             sleep 1
744:         done
745:     done
746: }
747: 
748: # ---- reboots from inside RouterOS -----------------------------------------
749: # /system reboot restarts RouterOS but not qemu or this container, and RouterOS
750: # can reject a NIC again on its way up. QEMU reports the reset as a RESET event
751: # on its second QMP monitor: check the data NICs again once RouterOS answers.
752: # The node stays ready during the reboot, as before; it loses the ready marker
753: # only when a NIC is still missing afterwards.
754: qmp_events() { # print QEMU's QMP events, one per line, while qemu runs
755:     # busybox nc exits when its stdin closes: hold it open for qemu's lifetime
756:     {
757:         printf '%s\n' '{"execute":"qmp_capabilities"}'
758:         while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 5; done
759:     } | nc 127.0.0.1 "$QMP_EVENT_PORT" 2>/dev/null
760: }
761: after_reboot() { # wait for RouterOS to answer, then check the data NICs again
762:     log "RouterOS rebooted: checking the data NICs again"
763:     sleep 5
764:     _t0=$(date +%s)
765:     until rest "$AUTH" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; do
766:         if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
767:             log "RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s after the reboot: data NICs not checked"
768:             return
769:         fi
770:         sleep 2
771:     done
772:     if check_data_nics; then
773:         touch "$READY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
774:         log "data NICs after the reboot: all $max are RouterOS interfaces"
775:     else
776:         rm -f "$READY_FILE"
777:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # a list of indices
778:         log "data NIC check FAILED after a reboot: RouterOS has no interface for $(ether_names $miss)(of $max data NICs)"
779:     fi
780: }
781: watch_reboots() { # in the background: check the data NICs after every reboot
782:     _last=0
783:     qmp_events | while read -r _ev; do
784:         case "$_ev" in *'"event": "RESET"'*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
785:         # One reboot resets the guest twice, milliseconds apart: handle it once.
786:         _ts=$(printf '%s' "$_ev" | sed -n 's/.*"seconds": *\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
787:         [ "${_ts:-0}" -gt $((_last + 10)) ] || continue
788:         _last=$_ts
789:         after_reboot
790:     done &
791: }
792: 
793: # Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. On a
794: # restart the CHR disk keeps its config and the marker (in the container rw
795: # layer) survives, so the bootstrap (which could wait forever if the config
796: # disabled `www` or changed the account, or reject duplicate `add` lines) is
797: # skipped. A fresh deploy recreates the container and the disk, so the marker
798: # and the config are both gone and the bootstrap runs.
799: if [ -f "$DONE_MARKER" ]; then
800:     log "already bootstrapped (restart): skipping config"
801:     mgmt_setup
802:     mgmt_attach
803:     ready
804:     watch_reboots
805:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
806:     exit 0
807: fi
808: 
809: # ---- credentials + identity -----------------------------------------------
810: # Every credential-establishing call is CHECKED: the ready marker never
811: # advertises credentials that do not work.
812: FACTORY="admin:"
813: rest "$FACTORY" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 || FACTORY="admin:$PASSWORD"
814: if [ "$USERNAME" = "admin" ]; then
815:     if [ -n "$PASSWORD" ]; then
816:         out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/set \
817:             "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\"}")"
818:         is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set admin password: ${out:-no response}"
819:     fi
820:     AUTH="admin:$PASSWORD"
821: else
822:     out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/add \
823:         "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$USERNAME")\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\",\"group\":\"full\"}")"
824:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}"
825:     AUTH="$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"
826:     # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the
827:     # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated
828:     # full-access account.
829:     out="$(rest "$AUTH" user/set "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}")"
830:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}"
831:     if rest "admin:" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then
832:         bootstrap_fail "factory admin still authenticates after disable"
833:     fi
834: fi
835: rest "$AUTH" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \
836:     || bootstrap_fail "the requested credentials do not authenticate"
837: out="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity/set "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$HOSTNAME_ARG")\"}")"
838: is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set identity: ${out:-no response}"
839: got="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity)"
840: case "$got" in
841:     *"\"name\":\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\""*) : ;;
842:     *) bootstrap_fail "identity not applied: ${got:-no response}" ;;
843: esac
844: 
845: mgmt_setup
846: discovery_setup
847: mgmt_attach
848: 
849: # ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------
850: if [ -s "$STARTUP_CFG" ]; then
851:     bridge_ll
852:     # one-shot HTTP server on the bridge's link-local address; the router
853:     # fetches from it through ether1 (fetch takes a zoned link-local address
854:     # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)
855:     {
856:         printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\n\r\n' \
857:             "$(wc -c < "$STARTUP_CFG")"
858:         cat "$STARTUP_CFG"
859:     } | timeout 90 nc -l -s "$LL%$MGMT_BR" -p "$FETCH_PORT" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
860:     sleep 1
861:     fetch="$(rest "$AUTH" tool/fetch \
862:         "{\"address\":\"$LL%ether1@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"port\":\"$FETCH_PORT\",\"src-path\":\"/config.auto.rsc\",\"mode\":\"http\",\"dst-path\":\"config.auto.rsc\"}")"
863:     case "$fetch" in
864:         *'"status":"finished"'*)
865:             # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets
866:             # CHR_BOOT_WAIT seconds.
867:             result="$(rest_raw "$AUTH" import '{"file-name":"config.auto.rsc"}' "$BOOT_WAIT")"
868:             case "$result" in
869:                 *'"ret":"true"'*)
870:                     log "startup config imported"
871:                     ;;
872:                 *)
873:                     # RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first
874:                     # error: the lines before it ARE applied.
875:                     detail="$(printf '%s' "$result" | sed -n 's/.*"detail":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
876:                     log "startup config import FAILED: ${detail:-${result:-no response}}; lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not"
877:                     wait "$QEMU_PID"
878:                     exit 0
879:                     ;;
880:             esac
881:             ;;
882:         *)
883:             log "startup config import FAILED: fetch did not finish: ${fetch:-no response}"
884:             wait "$QEMU_PID"
885:             exit 0
886:             ;;
887:     esac
888: fi
889: 
890: touch "$DONE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true
891: ready
892: watch_reboots
893: wait "$QEMU_PID"

check_data_nics; then\n539:     # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # a list of indices\n540:     log \"data NIC check FAILED: RouterOS has no interface for $(ether_names $miss)(of $max data NICs)\"\n541:     wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n542:     exit 0\n543: fi\n544: \n545: # Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST\n546: # answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the\n547: # configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.\n548: # A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is\n549: # logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).\n550: ssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc \"$VM_EP\" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }\n551: ready() {\n552:     case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/service?name=ssh\")\" in\n553:         *'\"disabled\":\"false\"'*)\n554:             _t0=$(date +%s)\n555:             until [ \"$(ssh_banner)\" = \"SSH-2.0\" ]; do\n556:                 if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n557:                     log \"SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)\"\n558:                     break\n559:                 fi\n560:                 sleep 2\n561:             done\n562:             ;;\n563:     esac\n564:     touch \"$READY_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n565:     log \"RouterOS ready\"\n566: }\n567: \n568: # A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can\n569: # still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).\n570: bootstrap_fail() {\n571:     log \"credential bootstrap FAILED: $1\"\n572:     wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n573:     exit 0\n574: }\n575: \n576: # ---- management: ether1 in its own VRF -------------------------------------\n577: # The VRF owns its routing table and connected routes. The link-local REST\n579: # channel survives the handoff once www and ether1 belong to the same VRF.\n580: mgmt_fail() {\n581:     log \"management setup FAILED: $1 (redeploy the node: containerlab deploy --reconfigure)\"\n582:     wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n583:     exit 0\n584: }\n585: rest_has() { # rest_has <path?query>: the GET answered a non-empty JSON array\n586:     case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\")\" in '['*'{'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac\n587: }\n588: rest_add() { # rest_add <what> <path> <json>: a 2xx with no error object, else mgmt_fail with the router's detail\n589:     _r=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" \"$2\" \"$3\" 20)\"\n590:     case \"$_r\" in\n591:         2??\\ *) is_err \"$_r\" && mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r#* }\" ;;\n592:         *) mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r:-no response}\" ;;\n593:     esac\n594: }\n595: rest_count() { # rest_count <path?query>: number of objects the GET answered\n596:     rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\" | tr '{' '\\n' | grep -c '\"\\.id\"'\n597: }\n598: rest_clear() { # rest_clear <menu>: remove its clab-mgmt objects\n599:     _ids=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" | tr '{' '\\n' \\\n600:         | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | paste -sd, -)\"\n601:     [ -z \"$_ids\" ] || rest_add \"remove old $1\" \"$1/remove\" \"{\\\".id\\\":\\\"$_ids\\\"}\"\n602: }\n603: # A native VRF creates its routing table asynchronously.
