Do not overwrite them on a restart.\n621:         [ -f \"$DONE_MARKER\" ] && return 0\n622:     else\n623:         if rest_has \"routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE\"; then\n624:             mgmt_fail \"table $MGMT_TABLE already exists without the launcher's VRF; use a fresh container\"\n625:         fi\n626:         _script=\":delay 1s; /ip vrf add name=$MGMT_TABLE interfaces=ether1 place-before=0 comment=$MGMT_COMMENT; /ip service set ssh,www,www-ssl,api,api-ssl,winbox,telnet vrf=$MGMT_TABLE; do\n631:         [ $(( $(date +%s) - _start )) -lt \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ] \\\n632:             || mgmt_fail \"VRF handoff did not complete; inspect RouterOS script errors through the serial console\"\n633:         sleep 1\n634:     done\n635:     log \"management VRF $MGMT_TABLE: ether1, routing table and service bindings verified\"\n636: }\n637: # The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with\n638: # the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.\n639: mgmt_in_place() {\n640:     _want=0\n641:     rest_has \"ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false\" || return 1\n642:     if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n648:         rest_has \"ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n649:         [ -z \"$G6\" ] || rest_has \"ipv6/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=::/0&gateway=$G6@$MGMT_TABLE\" || return 1\n650:         _want=$((_want + 1))\n651:     fi\n652:     [ \"$(rest_count \"ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")$(rest_count \"ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")\" \\\n653:         = \"$([ -n \"$M4\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n \"$M6\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)\" ] || return 1\n654:     rest_has \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none\" || return 1\n655:     [ \"$_want\" -gt 0 ]\n656: }\n657: mgmt_setup() {\n658:     mgmt_vrf\n659:     if mgmt_in_place; then\n660:         log \"management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}\"\n661:         return 0\n662:     fi\n663:     for _m in ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear \"$_m\"; then\n671:         rest_add \"ether1 address $M6\" ipv6/address/add \\\n672:             \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$M6\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"advertise\\\":\\\"no\\\",$_c}\"\n673:         [ -z \"$G6\" ] || rest_add \"IPv6 default via $G6 in VRF $MGMT_TABLE\" ipv6/route/add \\\n674:             \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"::/0\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"$G6@$MGMT_TABLE\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n675:     fi\n676:     _id=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/dhcp-client?interface=ether1\" | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n677:     [ -z \"$_id\" ] || rest_add \"disable the ether1 DHCP client\" ip/dhcp-client/set \\\n678:         \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"$_id\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}\"\n679:     # RouterOS's default ND entry (interface=all, ra-lifetime=30m) sends router\n680:     # advertisements on ether1 too, and every host on the management network\n681:     # with accept_ra would install the router as its IPv6 default route. An\n682:     # ether1 entry with ra-lifetime=none keeps the RAs harmless and withdraws a\n683:     # route a host already learned (a disabled entry does not override \"all\").\n684:     # /ipv6/nd keeps no comment, so its entry is found by interface.\n685:     _nd=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1\" | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n686:     if [ -n \"$_nd\" ]; then\n687:         rest_add \"ether1 router advertisements off\" ipv6/nd/set \\\n688:             \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"$_nd\\\",\\\"ra-lifetime\\\":\\\"none\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"no\\\"}\"\n689:     else\n690:         rest_add \"ether1 router advertisements off\" ipv6/nd/add \\\n691:             \"{\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"ra-lifetime\\\":\\\"none\\\"}\"\n692:     fi\n693:     # Prove they took (a transport flake answers an empty body, which is not\n694:     # an error by the set-contract).\n695:     if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n696:         rest_has \"ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4\" || mgmt_fail \"$M4 not on ether1\"\n697:     fi\n698:     mgmt_in_place || mgmt_fail \"management addressing or routes not applied\"\n699:     log \"management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in VRF $MGMT_TABLE\"\n700: }\n701: # Keep discovery on static data interfaces, excluding management. Set this only\n702: # on first boot, before attaching eth0: startup-config and subsequent user changes\n703: # can select a different list, and restarts must preserve that choice.\n704: discovery_setup() {\n705:     rest_add \"management interface list\" interface/list/add \\\n706:         \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"clab-management\\\",\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"}\"\n707:     rest_add \"management interface list member\" interface/list/member/add \\\n708:         \"{\\\"list\\\":\\\"clab-management\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"}\"\n709:     rest_add \"discovery interface list\" interface/list/add \\\n710:         \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"clab-discovery\\\",\\\"include\\\":\\\"static\\\",\\\"exclude\\\":\\\"clab-management\\\",\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"}\"\n711:     rest_add \"management discovery off\" ip/neighbor/discovery-settings/set \\\n712:         '{\"discover-interface-list\":\"clab-discovery\"}'\n713:     rest_has \"interface/list?name=clab-management&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" \\\n714:         || mgmt_fail \"management interface list not applied\"\n715:     rest_has \"interface/list/member?list=clab-management&interface=ether1&disabled=false&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" \\\n716:         || mgmt_fail \"management interface list member not applied\"\n717:     rest_has \"interface/list?name=clab-discovery&include=static&exclude=clab-management&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" \\\n718:         || mgmt_fail \"discovery interface list not applied\"\n719:     case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" ip/neighbor/discovery-settings)\" in\n720:         *'\"discover-interface-list\":\"clab-discovery\"'*) : ;;\n721:         *) mgmt_fail \"management discovery policy not applied\" ;;\n722:     esac\n723:     log \"neighbor discovery: static interfaces except ether1 (clab-discovery)\"\n724: }\n725: # Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the\n726: # management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request\n727: # refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC\n728: # before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).\n729: mgmt_attach() {\n730:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0\" ] || brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" eth0\n731:     ip link set eth0 up\n732:     for _pair in \"$G4 ${M4%/*}\" \"$G6 ${M6%/*}\"; do\n733:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # split \"gateway source\"; an empty half skips the pair\n734:         set -- $_pair\n735:         [ $# -eq 2 ] || continue\n736:         _t0=$(date +%s)\n737:         until case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" ping \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$1\\\",\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"$2\\\",\\\"count\\\":\\\"2\\\",\\\"vrf\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\"}\")\" in\n738:                 *'\"received\":\"'[1-9]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; do\n739:             if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then\n740:                 log \"gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)\"\n741:                 break\n742:             fi\n743:             sleep 1\n744:         done\n745:     done\n746: }\n747: \n748: # ---- reboots from inside RouterOS -----------------------------------------\n749: # /system reboot restarts RouterOS but not qemu or this container, and RouterOS\n750: # can reject a NIC again on its way up. QEMU reports the reset as a RESET event\n751: # on its second QMP monitor: check the data NICs again once RouterOS answers.\n752: # The node stays ready during the reboot, as before; it loses the ready marker\n753: # only when a NIC is still missing afterwards.\n754: qmp_events() { # print QEMU's QMP events, one per line, while qemu runs\n755:     # busybox nc exits when its stdin closes: hold it open for qemu's lifetime\n756:     {\n757:         printf '%s\\n' '{\"execute\":\"qmp_capabilities\"}'\n758:         while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 5; done\n759:     } | nc 127.0.0.1 \"$QMP_EVENT_PORT\" 2>/dev/null\n760: }\n761: after_reboot() { # wait for RouterOS to answer, then check the data NICs again\n762:     log \"RouterOS rebooted: checking the data NICs again\"\n763:     sleep 5\n764:     _t0=$(date +%s)\n765:     until rest \"$AUTH\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; do\n766:         if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n767:             log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s after the reboot: data NICs not checked\"\n768:             return\n769:         fi\n770:         sleep 2\n771:     done\n772:     if check_data_nics; then\n815:     if [ -n \"$PASSWORD\" ]; then\n816:         out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/set \\\n817:             \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\"}\")\"\n818:         is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set admin password: ${out:-no response}\"\n819:     fi\n820:     AUTH=\"admin:$PASSWORD\"\n821: else\n822:     out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/add \\\n823:         \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$USERNAME\")\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\",\\\"group\\\":\\\"full\\\"}\")\"\n824:     is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}\"\n825:     AUTH=\"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"\n826:     # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the\n827:     # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated\n828:     # full-access account.\n829:     out=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" user/set \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}\")\"\n830:     is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}\"\n831:     if rest \"admin:\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n832:         bootstrap_fail \"factory admin still authenticates after disable\"\n833:     fi\n834: fi\n835: rest \"$AUTH\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \\\n836:     || bootstrap_fail \"the requested credentials do not authenticate\"\n837: out=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity/set \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\")\\\"}\")\"\n838: is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set identity: ${out:-no response}\"\n839: got=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity)\"\n840: case \"$got\" in\n841:     *\"\\\"name\\\":\\\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\\\"\"*) : ;;\n842:     *) bootstrap_fail \"identity not applied: ${got:-no response}\" ;;\n843: esac\n844: \n845: mgmt_setup\n846: discovery_setup\n847: mgmt_attach\n848: \n849: # ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------\n850: if [ -s \"$STARTUP_CFG\" ]; then\n851:     bridge_ll\n852:     # one-shot HTTP server on the bridge's link-local address; the router\n853:     # fetches from it through ether1 (fetch takes a zoned link-local address\n854:     # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)\n855:     {\n856:         printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\\r\\nContent-Type: text/plain\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\n\\r\\n' \\\n857:             \"$(wc -c < \"$STARTUP_CFG\")\"\n858:         cat \"$STARTUP_CFG\"\n859:     } | timeout 90 nc -l -s \"$LL%$MGMT_BR\" -p \"$FETCH_PORT\" >/dev/null 2>&1 &\n860:     sleep 1\n861:     fetch=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" tool/fetch \\\n862:         \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$LL%ether1@$MGMT_TABLE\\\",\\\"port\\\":\\\"$FETCH_PORT\\\",\\\"src-path\\\":\\\"/config.auto.rsc\\\",\\\"mode\\\":\\\"http\\\",\\\"dst-path\\\":\\\"config.auto.rsc\\\"}\")\"\n863:     case \"$fetch\" in\n864:         *'\"status\":\"finished\"'*)\n865:             # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets\n866:             # CHR_BOOT_WAIT seconds.\n867:             result=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" import '{\"file-name\":\"config.auto.rsc\"}' \"$BOOT_WAIT\")\"\n868:             case \"$result\" in\n869:                 *'\"ret\":\"true\"'*)\n870:                     log \"startup config imported\"\n871:                     ;;\n872:                 *)\n873:                     # RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first\n874:                     # error: the lines before it ARE applied.\n875:                     detail=\"$(printf '%s' \"$result\" | sed -n 's/.*\"detail\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p')\"\n876:                     log \"startup config import FAILED: ${detail:-${result:-no response}}; check_data_nics; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # a list of indices\n    log \"data NIC check FAILED: RouterOS has no interface for $(ether_names $miss)(of $max data NICs)\"\n    wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n    exit 0\nfi\n\n# Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST\n# answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the\n# configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.\n# A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is\n# logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).\nssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc \"$VM_EP\" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }\nready() {\n    case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/service?name=ssh\")\" in\n        *'\"disabled\":\"false\"'*)\n            _t0=$(date +%s)\n            until [ \"$(ssh_banner)\" = \"SSH-2.0\" ]; do\n                if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n                    log \"SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)\"\n                    break\n                fi\n                sleep 2\n            done\n            ;;\n    esac\n    touch \"$READY_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    log \"RouterOS ready\"\n}\n\n# A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can\n# still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).\nbootstrap_fail() {\n    log \"credential bootstrap FAILED: $1\"\n    wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n    exit 0\n}\n\n# ---- management: ether1 in its own VRF -------------------------------------\n# The VRF owns its routing table and connected routes. 536: # Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST
537: # answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the
538: # configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.
539: # A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is
540: # logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).
541: ssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc "$VM_EP" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }
542: ready() {
543:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/service?name=ssh")" in
544:         *'"disabled":"false"'*)
545:             _t0=$(date +%s)
546:             until [ "$(ssh_banner)" = "SSH-2.0" ]; do
547:                 if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
548:                     log "SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)"
549:                     break
550:                 fi
551:                 sleep 2
552:             done
553:             ;;
554:     esac
555:     touch "$READY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
556:     log "RouterOS ready"
557: }

621:     until mgmt_vrf_ready; do
622:         [ $(( $(date +%s) - _start )) -lt "$BOOT_WAIT" ] \
623:             || mgmt_fail "VRF handoff did not complete; inspect RouterOS script errors through the serial console"
624:         sleep 1
625:     done
626:     log "management VRF $MGMT_TABLE: ether1, routing table and service bindings verified"
627: }
628: # The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with
629: # the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.
630: mgmt_in_place() {
631:     _want=0
632:     rest_has "ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false" || return 1
633:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
634:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
635:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_has "ip/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=0.0.0.0/0&gateway=$G4@$MGMT_TABLE" || return 1
636:         _want=$((_want + 1))
637:     fi
638:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
639:         rest_has "ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
640:         [ -z "$G6" ] || rest_has "ipv6/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=::/0&gateway=$G6@$MGMT_TABLE" || return 1
641:         _want=$((_want + 1))
642:     fi
643:     [ "$(rest_count "ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")$(rest_count "ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")" \
644:         = "$([ -n "$M4" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n "$M6" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" ] || return 1
645:     rest_has "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none" || return 1
646:     [ "$_want" -gt 0 ]
647: }
648: mgmt_setup() {
649:     mgmt_vrf
650:     if mgmt_in_place; then
651:         log "management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}"
652:         return 0
653:     fi
654:     for _m in ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear "$_m"; done
655:     _c="\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\""
656:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
657:         rest_add "ether1 address $M4" ip/address/add "{\"address\":\"$M4\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",$_c}"
658:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_add "default via $G4 in VRF $MGMT_TABLE" ip/route/add \
659:             "{\"dst-address\":\"0.0.0.0/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G4@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
660:     fi
661:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
662:         rest_add "ether1 address $M6" ipv6/address/add \
663:             "{\"address\":\"$M6\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"advertise\":\"no\",$_c}"
664:         [ -z "$G6" ] || rest_add "IPv6 default via $G6 in VRF $MGMT_TABLE" ipv6/route/add \
665:             "{\"dst-address\":\"::/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G6@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
666:     fi
667:     _id="$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/dhcp-client?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
668:     [ -z "$_id" ] || rest_add "disable the ether1 DHCP client" ip/dhcp-client/set \
669:         "{\"numbers\":\"$_id\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}"
670:     # RouterOS's default ND entry (interface=all, ra-lifetime=30m) sends router
671:     # advertisements on ether1 too, and every host on the management network
672:     # with accept_ra would install the router as its IPv6 default route. An
673:     # ether1 entry with ra-lifetime=none keeps the RAs harmless and withdraws a
674:     # route a host already learned (a disabled entry does not override "all").
675:     # /ipv6/nd keeps no comment, so its entry is found by interface.
676:     _nd="$(rest "$AUTH" "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
677:     if [ -n "$_nd" ]; then
678:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/set \
679:             "{\"numbers\":\"$_nd\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\",\"disabled\":\"no\"}"
680:     else
681:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/add \
682:             "{\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\"}"
683:     fi
684:     # Prove they took (a transport flake answers an empty body, which is not
685:     # an error by the set-contract).
686:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
687:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4" || mgmt_fail "$M4 not on ether1"
688:     fi
689:     mgmt_in_place || mgmt_fail "management addressing or routes not applied"
690:     log "management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in VRF $MGMT_TABLE"
691: }
692: # Keep discovery on static data interfaces, excluding management. Set this only
693: # on first boot, before attaching eth0: startup-config and subsequent user changes
694: # can select a different list, and restarts must preserve that choice.
695: discovery_setup() {
696:     rest_add "management interface list" interface/list/add \
697:         "{\"name\":\"clab-management\",\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\"}"
698:     rest_add "management interface list member" interface/list/member/add \
699:         "{\"list\":\"clab-management\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\"}"
700:     rest_add "discovery interface list" interface/list/add \
701:         "{\"name\":\"clab-discovery\",\"include\":\"static\",\"exclude\":\"clab-management\",\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\"}"
702:     rest_add "management discovery off" ip/neighbor/discovery-settings/set \
703:         '{"discover-interface-list":"clab-discovery"}'
704:     rest_has "interface/list?name=clab-management&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" \
705:         || mgmt_fail "management interface list not applied"
706:     rest_has "interface/list/member?list=clab-management&interface=ether1&disabled=false&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" \
707:         || mgmt_fail "management interface list member not applied"
708:     rest_has "interface/list?name=clab-discovery&include=static&exclude=clab-management&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" \
709:         || mgmt_fail "discovery interface list not applied"
710:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" ip/neighbor/discovery-settings)" in
711:         *'"discover-interface-list":"clab-discovery"'*) : ;;
712:         *) mgmt_fail "management discovery policy not applied" ;;
713:     esac
714:     log "neighbor discovery: static interfaces except ether1 (clab-discovery)"
715: }
716: # Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the
717: # management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request
718: # refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC
719: # before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).
720: mgmt_attach() {
721:     [ -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0" ] || brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" eth0
722:     ip link set eth0 up
723:     for _pair in "$G4 ${M4%/*}" "$G6 ${M6%/*}"; do
724:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # split "gateway source"; an empty half skips the pair
725:         set -- $_pair
726:         [ $# -eq 2 ] || continue
727:         _t0=$(date +%s)
728:         until case "$(rest "$AUTH" ping "{\"address\":\"$1\",\"src-address\":\"$2\",\"count\":\"2\",\"vrf\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\"}")" in
729:                 *'"received":"'[1-9]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; do
730:             if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then
731:                 log "gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)"
732:                 break
733:             fi
734:             sleep 1
735:         done
736:     done
737: }
738: 
739: # Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. On a
740: # restart the CHR disk keeps its config and the marker (in the container rw
741: # layer) survives, so the bootstrap (which could wait forever if the config
742: # disabled `www` or changed the account, or reject duplicate `add` lines) is
743: # skipped. A fresh deploy recreates the container and the disk, so the marker
744: # and the config are both gone and the bootstrap runs.
745: if [ -f "$DONE_MARKER" ]; then
746:     log "already bootstrapped (restart): skipping config"
747:     mgmt_setup
748:     mgmt_attach
749:     ready
750:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
751:     exit 0
752: fi
753: 
754: # ---- credentials + identity -----------------------------------------------
755: # Every credential-establishing call is CHECKED: the ready marker never
756: # advertises credentials that do not work.
757: FACTORY="admin:"
758: rest "$FACTORY" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 || FACTORY="admin:$PASSWORD"
759: if [ "$USERNAME" = "admin" ]; then
760:     if [ -n "$PASSWORD" ]; then
761:         out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/set \
762:             "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\"}")"
763:         is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set admin password: ${out:-no response}"
764:     fi
765:     AUTH="admin:$PASSWORD"
766: else
767:     out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/add \
768:         "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$USERNAME")\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\",\"group\":\"full\"}")"
769:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}"
770:     AUTH="$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"
771:     # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the
772:     # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated
773:     # full-access account.
774:     out="$(rest "$AUTH" user/set "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}")"
775:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}"
776:     if rest "admin:" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then
777:         bootstrap_fail "factory admin still authenticates after disable"
778:     fi
779: fi
780: rest "$AUTH" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \
781:     || bootstrap_fail "the requested credentials do not authenticate"
782: out="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity/set "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$HOSTNAME_ARG")\"}")"
783: is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set identity: ${out:-no response}"
784: got="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity)"
785: case "$got" in
786:     *"\"name\":\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\""*) : ;;
787:     *) bootstrap_fail "identity not applied: ${got:-no response}" ;;
788: esac
789: 
790: mgmt_setup
791: discovery_setup
792: mgmt_attach
793: 
794: # ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------
795: if [ -s "$STARTUP_CFG" ]; then
796:     bridge_ll
797:     # one-shot HTTP server on the bridge's link-local address; the router
798:     # fetches from it through ether1 (fetch takes a zoned link-local address
799:     # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)
800:     {
801:         printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\n\r\n' \
802:             "$(wc -c < "$STARTUP_CFG")"
803:         cat "$STARTUP_CFG"
804:     } | timeout 90 nc -l -s "$LL%$MGMT_BR" -p "$FETCH_PORT" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
805:     sleep 1
806:     fetch="$(rest "$AUTH" tool/fetch \
807:         "{\"address\":\"$LL%ether1@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"port\":\"$FETCH_PORT\",\"src-path\":\"/config.auto.rsc\",\"mode\":\"http\",\"dst-path\":\"config.auto.rsc\"}")"
808:     case "$fetch" in
809:         *'"status":"finished"'*)
810:             # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets
811:             # CHR_BOOT_WAIT seconds.
812:             result="$(rest_raw "$AUTH" import '{"file-name":"config.auto.rsc"}' "$BOOT_WAIT")"
813:             case "$result" in
814:                 *'"ret":"true"'*)
815:                     log "startup config imported"
816:                     ;;
817:                 *)
818:                     # RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first
819:                     # error: the lines before it ARE applied.
820:                     detail="$(printf '%s' "$result" | sed -n 's/.*"detail":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
821:                     log "startup config import FAILED: ${detail:-${result:-no response}}; lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not"
822:                     wait "$QEMU_PID"
823:                     exit 0
824:                     ;;
825:             esac
826:             ;;
827:         *)
828:             log "startup config import FAILED: fetch did not finish: ${fetch:-no response}"
829:             wait "$QEMU_PID"
830:             exit 0
831:             ;;
832:     esac
833: fi
834: 
835: touch "$DONE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true
836: ready
837: wait "$QEMU_PID"

**Defect candidate 21 — Missing: `PCI_BRIDGES=0` (arm64) path: re-plug loop only runs when `PCI_BRIDGES = 1`. So on arm64, `check_data_nics` after reboot will fail if a NIC is missing (no re-plug on arm64), matching boot behavior. Fine.

Now, the more subtle correctness question: **does QEMU's RESET event actually fire for a guest-initiated reboot?** Yes — QMP RESET event is emitted when the guest requests a system reset (triple fault, ACPI reset, `/system reboot`). Good.

**Another candidate — the `after_reboot` READY_FILE touch: on success it touches the ready file. But consider the *bootstrap-failed* case: watch_reboots isn't started (fail paths exit before). Fine.

**Another candidate — `watch_reboots` background job and `set -u`: `_ev`, `_ts`, `_last` all defined. Fine.

**Another candidate — busybox `nc` availability of `-s`/`-p` used elsewhere; plain `nc 127.0.0.1 $QMP_EVENT_PORT` fine.

**Another candidate — In `qmp_events`, the printf emits qmp_capabilities, then the loop sleeps 5s in iterations. But QMP server expects a newline-terminated command — provided.

Now the **test file**: let me read head tests/16-mikrotik-chr/02-chr-high-ports.robot fully to check the new test and its keywords, and whether `Login via SSH with username and password` keyword exists in that suite or a shared resource. Also check that `High port forwards traffic` requires data path after reboot. Also `Node is healthy` keyword.

Also there's a potential test-design issue: after `/system reboot`, RouterOS restarts, and the test immediately closes connection and sleeps 20s, then waits for traffic forwarding. But during reboot the ready marker stays; `Node is healthy` would pass trivially. The meaningful assertion is `High port forwards traffic` within 300s. That's fine.

But one issue: `SSHLibrary.Start Command /system reboot` — after starting reboot, closing connection. The reboot kills SSH daemon; Start Command may hang? Start Command executes and returns output immediately without waiting for completion? In Robot SSHLibrary, `Start Command` starts a command and `Read Command Output` reads later; it doesn't block on completion. Closing the connection then is fine.

Now check the docs file head version for the changed paragraph — already seen in diff; doc line 82 in head. Fine.

16: // launcherFunction isolates a shell function without running the disk, network,
17: // QEMU or REST operations at the top level of the embedded launcher.
18: // It assumes nested closing braces are indented; a nested brace at column zero
19: // would be mistaken for the end of the function.
20: func launcherFunction(t *testing.T, name string) string {
21: 	t.Helper()
22: 
23: 	_, body, ok := strings.Cut(string(launcherScript), "\n"+name+"() {")
24: 	if !ok {
25: 		t.Fatalf("launcher function %q not found", name)
26: 	}
27: 	body, _, ok = strings.Cut(body, "\n}\n")
28: 	if !ok {
29: 		t.Fatalf("launcher function %q has no closing brace", name)
30: 	}
31: 
32: 	return name + "() {" + body + "\n}\n"
33: }
34: 
35: func TestLauncherShellSyntax(t *testing.T) {
36: 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "/bin/sh", "-n")
37: 	cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(string(launcherScript))
38: 	if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
39: 		t.Fatalf("invalid launcher shell syntax: %v\n%s", err, out)
40: 	}
41: }

156: func TestCheckNICIndex(t *testing.T) {
157: 	tests := map[string]struct {
158: 		pciBridges int
159: 		index      int
160: 		errText    string // empty when the index is accepted
161: 	}{
162: 		"bridges-zero":      {pciBridges: 1, index: 0},
163: 		"bridges-old-limit": {pciBridges: 1, index: 28},
164: 		"bridges-ether33":   {pciBridges: 1, index: 32},
165: 		"bridges-max":       {pciBridges: 1, index: 63},
166: 		"bridges-over":      {pciBridges: 1, index: 64, errText: "beyond the tested limit"},
167: 		"bridges-mac-wrap":  {pciBridges: 1, index: 256, errText: "beyond the tested limit"},
168: 		"no-bridges-max":    {pciBridges: 0, index: 29},
169: 		"no-bridges-full":   {pciBridges: 0, index: 30, errText: "no PCI slot for the disk"},
170: 		"no-bridges-high":   {pciBridges: 0, index: 256, errText: "no PCI slot for the disk"},
171: 	}
172: 
173: 	fn := launcherFunction(t, "check_nic_index")
174: 	for name, tc := range tests {
175: 		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
176: 			cmd := exec.CommandContext(
177: 				t.Context(),
178: 				"/bin/sh",
179: 				"-c",
180: 				"log() { printf '%s\\n' \"$*\" >&2; }\n"+fn+
181: 					"PCI_BRIDGES=\"$1\"; check_nic_index \"$2\"",
182: 				"chr-launch-test",
183: 				fmt.Sprint(tc.pciBridges),
184: 				fmt.Sprint(tc.index),
185: 			)
186: 			out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
187: 			if tc.errText == "" {
188: 				if err != nil {
189: 					t.Fatalf("index %d rejected: %v\n%s", tc.index, err, out)
190: 				}
191: 				return
192: 			}
193: 			if err == nil || !strings.Contains(string(out), tc.errText) {
194: 				t.Errorf(
195: 					"index %d: want error containing %q, got %v: %s",
196: 					tc.index,
197: 					tc.errText,
198: 					err,
199: 					out,
200: 				)
201: 			}
202: 		})

1: // Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
2: // Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
3: // SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
4: 
5: // Package mikrotik_chr runs MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the official mikrotik/chr image.
6: //
7: // The image is MikroTik's own distribution (Alpine + qemu + the CHR disk) and is used
8: // unmodified: the kind writes chr-launch.sh into the node's lab directory, bind-mounts it
9: // read-only and sets it as the entrypoint in place of the image's /start.sh, which is not
10: // orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116, #3464).
11: package mikrotik_chr
12: 
13: import (
14: 	"context"
15: 	_ "embed"
16: 	"errors"
17: 	"fmt"
18: 	"net"
19: 	"os"
20: 	"path"
21: 	"path/filepath"
22: 	"regexp"
23: 	"runtime"
24: 	"slices"
25: 	"strconv"
26: 	"strings"
27: 
28: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
29: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
30: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
31: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
32: )
33: 
34: var (
35: 	kindNames          = []string{"mikrotik_chr"}
36: 	defaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials("admin", "admin")
37: 
38: 	InterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`ether(?P<port>\d+)`)
39: 	InterfaceOffset = 2
40: 	InterfaceHelp   = "etherX (where X >= 2) or ethX (where X >= 1)"
41: 
42: 	//go:embed chr-launch.sh
43: 	launcherScript []byte
44: )
45: 
46: const (
47: 	configDirName   = "ftpboot"
48: 	startupCfgFName = "config.auto.rsc"
49: 
50: 	launcherFName = "chr-launch.sh"
51: 	launcherPath  = "/chr-launch.sh"
52: 	// readyFile is written by the launcher once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the
53: 	// startup config, and removed at every container start.
54: 	readyFile = "/.chr-launch-ready"
55: 
56: 	// mgmtComment tags every management object the launcher creates in RouterOS.
57: 	mgmtComment = "clab-mgmt"
58: 
59: 	// amd64's tested PCI-bridge layout. Beyond it the guest runs out of interrupt
60: 	// vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS out of PCI I/O space (8 bridges).
61: 	maxDataNICIndex = 63
62: 	// arm64's virt machine gets no PCI bridges: its single bus holds the disk, the
63: 	// management NIC and at most 29 data NICs before QEMU runs out of slots.
64: 	maxDataNICIndexARM64 = 29
65: 
66: 	// the launcher's CHR_INTF_WAIT and CHR_BOOT_WAIT defaults, and the time its config
67: 	// fetch and gateway check add, in seconds.
68: 	defaultIntfWait  = 60
69: 	defaultBootWait  = 300
70: 	startPeriodSlack = 90
71: 	// the launcher's wait for the interface list to settle and its re-plug rounds, in seconds.
72: 	replugWait = 180
73: 
74: 	scrapliPlatformName = "mikrotik_routeros" //nolint: misspell
75: )
76: 
77: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
78: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
79: 	platformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{
80: 		ScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs)
84: 
85: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
86: 		return new(mikrotikCHR)
87: 	}, nrea)
88: }
89: 
90: type mikrotikCHR struct {
91: 	clabnodes.VRNode
92: 	// goarch selects the NIC layout the interface limit is checked against. The
93: 	// containerlab binary's architecture matches the image's outside emulated setups.
94: 	goarch string
95: }
96: 
97: func (n *mikrotikCHR) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
98: 	n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)
99: 	n.ConfigDirName = configDirName
100: 	n.StartupCfgFName = startupCfgFName
101: 	// The image's qemu falls back to TCG emulation without /dev/kvm: KVM makes the boot
102: 	// fast but is not required.
103: 	n.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = false
104: 
105: 	n.Cfg = cfg
106: 	for _, o := range opts {
107: 		o(n)
108: 	}
109: 
110: 	// Credentials travel as env, not on the command line, so a password needs no quoting.
111: 	defEnv := map[string]string{
112: 		"USERNAME": n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
113: 		"PASSWORD": n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
114: 	}
115: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)
116: 
117: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,
118: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, configDirName), ":/ftpboot"),
119: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName), ":", launcherPath, ":ro"),
120: 	)

154: // CheckInterfaceName rejects data NIC indices the launcher does not create: beyond the
155: // tested PCI-bridge layout on amd64, or the free PCI slots on arm64.
156: func (n *mikrotikCHR) CheckInterfaceName() error {
157: 	if err := n.VRNode.CheckInterfaceName(); err != nil {
158: 		return err
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	limit := dataNICLimit(n.goarch)
162: 	for _, ep := range n.Endpoints {
163: 		ifName := ep.GetIfaceName()

172: 			return fmt.Errorf(

175: 			)
176: 		}

191: }

193: // startPeriod is the healthcheck start period in seconds: the launcher's own worst case
194: // before the ready file, so a slow boot (TCG) never reports unhealthy. It waits up to
195: // CHR_INTF_WAIT for the links, then up to CHR_BOOT_WAIT each for REST, the VRF
196: // handoff, the startup-config import and the SSH banner, plus fetch and gateway checks
197: // and re-plugging NICs RouterOS rejected.
198: func startPeriod(env map[string]string) int {
199: 	return envSeconds(env, "CHR_INTF_WAIT", defaultIntfWait) +
200: 		4*envSeconds(env, "CHR_BOOT_WAIT", defaultBootWait) + startPeriodSlack + replugWait
201: }

233: // SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS

235: // without the objects the launcher creates at every boot. Explicit discovery=static

238: func (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(_ context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {

246: 			`:put ("/ip service set [find where name=" . [/ip service get $s name] . " dynamic=no] vrf=main")}; `+
247: 			`:if ([/snmp get vrf] = "main") do={:put "/snmp set vrf=main"}`,
248: 	)
249: 	if err != nil {
250: 		return nil, err
251: 	}
252: 
253: 	return clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,
254: 		[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+"\n"))
255: }

257: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
258: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt VRF,
259: // its default routes and the discovery lists), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1
260: // DHCP client. Imported again as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the
261: // launcher already created and RouterOS stops the import at the first one; management addressing
262: // belongs to
263: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
264: // before matching.
265: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
266: 	var out []string
267: 
268: 	section := ""
269: 	pending := ""
270: 	keymatHeader := ""
271: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
272: 		if pending != "" {
273: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
274: 			pending = ""
275: 		}
276: 		if continues(line) {
277: 			pending = line
278: 			continue
279: 		}
280: 
281: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
282: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
283: 			section = trimmed
284: 			keymatHeader = ""
285: 			// Older RouterOS releases reject even an empty keymat menu. Emit
286: 			// its header only if a command remains after filtering below.
287: 			if section == "/system keymat-provider" {
288: 				keymatHeader = line
289: 				continue
290: 			}
291: 		}
292: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
293: 			continue
294: 		}
295: 		// Repeated RouterOS exports can include this disabled factory QKD
296: 		// placeholder. Fresh imports reject it (duplicate name or empty KME
297: 		// address). Drop only this exact entry; keep configured providers.
298: 		if section == "/system keymat-provider" &&
299: 			strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(trimmed, `\`, "")), " ") ==
300: 				"add disabled=yes key-size=0 name=default qkd-cache-size=0 qkd-certificate=*0 type=qkd" {
301: 			continue
302: 		}
303: 		if keymatHeader != "" && trimmed != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
304: 			out = append(out, keymatHeader)
305: 			keymatHeader = ""
306: 		}
307: 		out = append(out, line)
308: 	}
309: 	if pending != "" {
310: 		if keymatHeader != "" {
311: 			out = append(out, keymatHeader)
312: 		}
313: 		out = append(out, pending)
314: 	}
315: 
316: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
317: }
318: 
319: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
320: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
321: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
322: func continues(line string) bool {
323: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
324: 
325: 	return trailing%2 == 1
326: }
327: 
328: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
329: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
330: 		return false
331: 	}
332: 
333: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
334: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
335: 
336: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
337: 		return true
338: 	}
339: 
340: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
341: 	switch section {
342: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
343: 		return has("interface=ether1")
344: 	}
345: 
346: 	return false
347: }

Reasoning
Now I have a good picture. Let me also double-check a couple of remaining items:

1. The `set -u` interplay with `_ts` — `[ "${_ts:-0}" -gt $((_last + 10)) ]` handles unset. But in the `_ts=$(...)` assignment, if sed finds nothing, `_ts` is empty → handled by `${_ts:-0}` → 0 → skip. Good.

2. One thing I want to verify: in `watch_reboots`, the `&` backgrounds the pipeline; but the `qmp_events` writer subshell does `while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID"` — QEMU_PID is set. Good.

3. A significant one I should think about: **`after_reboot` runs inside the reader subshell of a pipeline under `set -u`. `_miss`? No.** Fine.

4. **`check_data_nics` references `$PCI_BRIDGES`, `$max`, `$miss` — all set.**

5. Now think about **a real failure mode: `watch_reboots` background job is started but the main script's `wait "$QEMU_PID"` only waits for qemu. When qemu dies, main exits 0, container stops. The background watcher processes die with the container. Fine.

Reasoning
Confirmed: the only test change is the added "Ensure a reboot from inside RouterOS keeps all interfaces" test case.

One design point worth checking: the test's meaningful assertions are:
1. After reboot, `/interface ethernet print count-only` returns 64 (so ether64 survived the reboot).
2. Ping across ether64 works.
3. `Node is healthy r1`.

Note the test's weakness: the reboot may not have completed within the 300s window in a way that exercises the failure path — but if the reboot never happened, ether64 would still be present (from before the reboot), so the test would pass vacuously. 748: # ---- reboots from inside RouterOS -----------------------------------------
749: # /system reboot restarts RouterOS but not qemu or this container, and RouterOS
750: # can reject a NIC again on its way up. QEMU reports the reset as a RESET event
751: # on its second QMP monitor: check the data NICs again once RouterOS answers.
752: # The node stays ready during the reboot, as before; it loses the ready marker
753: # only when a NIC is still missing afterwards.
754: qmp_events() { # print QEMU's QMP events, one per line, while qemu runs
755:     # busybox nc exits when its stdin closes: hold it open for qemu's lifetime
756:     {
757:         printf '%s\n' '{"execute":"qmp_capabilities"}'
758:         while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 5; done
759:     } | nc 127.0.0.1 "$QMP_EVENT_PORT" 2>/dev/null
760: }
761: after_reboot() { # wait for RouterOS to answer, then check the data NICs again
762:     log "RouterOS rebooted: checking the data NICs again"
763:     sleep 5
764:     _t0=$(date +%s)
765:     until rest "$AUTH" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; do
766:         if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
767:             log "RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s after the reboot: data NICs not checked"
768:             return
769:         fi
770:         sleep 2
771:     done
772:     if check_data_nics; then
773:         touch "$READY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
774:         log "data NICs after the reboot: all $max are RouterOS interfaces"
775:     else
776:         rm -f "$READY_FILE"
777:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # a list of indices
778:         log "data NIC check FAILED after a reboot: RouterOS has no interface for $(ether_names $miss)(of $max data NICs)"
779:     fi
780: }
781: watch_reboots() { # in the background: check the data NICs after every reboot
782:     _last=0
783:     qmp_events | while read -r _ev; do
784:         case "$_ev" in *'"event": "RESET"'*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
785:         # One reboot resets the guest twice, milliseconds apart: handle it once.
786:         _ts=$(printf '%s' "$_ev" | sed -n 's/.*"seconds": *\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
787:         [ "${_ts:-0}" -gt $((_last + 10)) ] || continue
788:         _last=$_ts
789:         after_reboot
790:     done &
791: }
792: 
793: # Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. On a
794: # restart the CHR disk keeps its config and the marker (in the container rw
795: # layer) survives, so the bootstrap (which could wait forever if the config
796: # disabled `www` or changed the account, or reject duplicate `add` lines) is
797: # skipped. A fresh deploy recreates the container and the disk, so the marker
798: # and the config are both gone and the bootstrap runs.
799: if [ -f "$DONE_MARKER" ]; then
800:     log "already bootstrapped (restart): skipping config"
801:     mgmt_setup
802:     mgmt_attach
803:     ready
804:     watch_reboots
805:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
806:     exit 0
807: fi
808: 
809: # ---- credentials + identity -----------------------------------------------
810: # Every credential-establishing call is CHECKED: the ready marker never
811: # advertises credentials that do not work.
812: FACTORY="admin:"
813: rest "$FACTORY" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 || FACTORY="admin:$PASSWORD"
814: if [ "$USERNAME" = "admin" ]; then
815:     if [ -n "$PASSWORD" ]; then
816:         out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/set \
817:             "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\"}")"
818:         is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set admin password: ${out:-no response}"
819:     fi
820:     AUTH="admin:$PASSWORD"
821: else
822:     out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/add \
823:         "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$USERNAME")\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\",\"group\":\"full\"}")"

do sleep 5; done\n    } | nc 127.0.0.1 \"$QMP_EVENT_PORT\" 2>/dev/null\n}\nafter_reboot() { # wait for RouterOS to answer, then check the data NICs again\n    log \"RouterOS rebooted: checking the data NICs again\"\n    sleep 5\n    _t0=$(date +%s)\n    until rest \"$AUTH\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; The refactor is faithful: base's inline stabilization loop, re-plug loop, and failure handling become `check_data_nics()`, with the same logic and `$miss` preserved. One behavioral nuance: in base, the failure path ended with `wait "$QEMU_PID"; exit 0`; in head, `check_data_nics` returns 1 and the caller at line 538-543 does the same. Faithful.

Another subtle refactor nuance: in base, `[ "$_round" -gt 1 ] && log ...` ran only on success path (after the failure `if` exited). In head, `check_data_nics` returns 1 early if miss non-empty, so the success log only runs on success too. Faithful.

Now, let me look at one more thing I haven't fully verified: where the initial RESET vs `check_data_nics` interaction happens. The watcher starts *after* the first `check_data_nics` and `ready` (both paths). Since the event monitor only delivers events to connected clients, the boot-time RESETs (SeaBIOS/edk2) aren't seen. Good.

Also — one more potential issue: **the QMP event monitor connection is established when `watch_reboots` runs. But `qmp_events`'s nc connects and *holds* the connection. Meanwhile, `after_reboot` calls `qmp()` which connects to QMP_PORT (5001) — a different monitor. Fine.

Now — a genuinely important check I haven't done: **does QEMU support two `-qmp` monitors?** Yes — each `-qmp` option adds a separate chardev+monitor. Well-known QEMU feature (e.g., libvirt uses multiple monitors). Confirmed OK in the prior session.

Next: verify the header comment at the top of the script mentions port 5002 (docs for operators). Let me check the header around lines 40-60 for the port list comment. Earlier summary said ports: 5000 serial, 5001 QMP control, 8080 fetch. If the header lists exposed ports and doesn't mention 5002, that's a minor doc gap in the script header. Line 51 mentions 5000 (serial console). Let me check whether the header mentions 5001 and whether 5002 should be there. Also the doc page (mikrotik_chr.md) may list ports exposed by the node — worth checking.

Also, is QMP_EVENT_PORT bound to 127.0.0.1 only? Yes, tcp:127.0.0.1:5002 — inside the container's netns. Not exposed to the host unless the topology publishes it. Fine.

Let me read the header and the doc's port mentions.

20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred
21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,
22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container
23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps
24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is
25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,
26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return
27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches
28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)
29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it
30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu
31: #
32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an
33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW
34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never
35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is
36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are
37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu
38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and
39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management
40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.
41: #
42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,
43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.
44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]
45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env
46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the
47: #   official image's own variables:
48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),
49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)
50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container
51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no
52: #   address on the management network.
53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default
54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.
55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed "chr-launch:":
56: #   "RouterOS ready"                   login + startup config done
57: #   "startup config import FAILED: …"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's
58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)
59: #   "credential bootstrap FAILED: …"   the user/password step failed
60: #   "management setup FAILED: …"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed
61: #   "data NIC check FAILED: …"         RouterOS lacks an interface for a data NIC
62: #                                      even after re-plugging it (also checked
63: #                                      after a reboot from inside RouterOS)
64: #
65: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
66: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
67: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
68: 
69: set -u
70: 
71: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting
72: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.
73: USERNAME="${USERNAME:-admin}"
74: PASSWORD="${PASSWORD-admin}"
75: HOSTNAME_ARG=""
76: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
77:     case "$1" in
78:         --username) USERNAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79:         --password) PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
80:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
81:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;
82:         --trace) shift ;;
83:         *) shift ;;
84:     esac
85: done
86: [ -n "$HOSTNAME_ARG" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG="$(hostname)"
87: 
88: CPUS="${CPUS:-1}"
89: DISK="${DISK:-128M}"
90: INTF_WAIT="${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}"
91: BOOT_WAIT="${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}"
92: INTFS="${CLAB_INTFS:-0}"
93: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc
94: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the
95: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).
96: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped
97: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready
98: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id
99: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics

  Line 67: Data ports start at `ether2`: `ether1` is the management interface. Using `ether1` in a topology results in an error.

  Line 72: On AMD64, data NICs are placed behind PCI bridges rather than sharing the default PC's root bus with all other devices. This removes the default layout's limit of 29 total Ethernet interfaces (management plus 28 data ports), so links can use `ether30` and higher without a custom launcher. ARM64 still uses a single PCI bus on the `virt` machine, shared with the disk and the management NIC; the PCI-bridge expansion applies only to AMD64.

  Line 78: * AMD64: `eth63` / `ether64`, the highest port tested. More interfaces exhaust the guest's interrupt vectors (with the default single vCPU) and, from about 200, the virtual PC firmware's PCI address space, which stops the VM before RouterOS boots.

  Line 79: * ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus.

  Line 84: With more than about 30 data ports, RouterOS can reject a NIC while it boots, and the interface does not appear. The launcher checks that RouterOS has an interface for every data NIC and re-plugs the missing ones before the node reports ready; RouterOS keeps their configuration. It checks again after RouterOS reboots itself (for example with `/system reboot`), when the container keeps running. If a NIC is still missing, the launcher logs `data NIC check FAILED` and the node is not healthy.

  Line 86: Sparse interface numbering also consumes VM resources for the intervening ports; memory defaults scale with the highest index, not just the number of links.

  Line 94: A RouterOS script (`.rsc`) set with [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) is imported once the router is up:

  Line 106: The file is copied to the node's lab directory as `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` and imported over the REST API. RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first error: in that case the container log carries RouterOS's own reason with the line number, for example

  Line 109: chr-launch: startup config import FAILED: Script Error: bad parameter network-type (line 3 column 59); lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not

  Line 116: [`containerlab save`](../../cmd/save.md) writes each node's `/export` to `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` in its lab directory. The save filter omits `add` entries tagged `clab-mgmt`, plus IPv4/IPv6 address, DHCP-client and IPv6 neighbor-discovery `add` entries for `ether1`, even without that tag. These management settings belong to the deployment and are recreated by the launcher; custom entries in those `ether1` sections are also omitted. Other interfaces and untagged configuration in other sections are preserved.

  Line 118: Saving explicitly retains an intentional `discover-interface-list=static` choice, which RouterOS normally omits as its default, so it survives redeployment. The launcher-owned discovery lists are recreated before the saved configuration is imported.

  Line 122: Repeated exports on RouterOS 7.24.5, 7.25, 7.25rc3 and 7.26beta4 can include an empty, disabled default `/system keymat-provider` entry that fails to import on a fresh router. Configured default providers and custom providers are preserved. RouterOS 7.23.8 does not emit the entry.

850: if [ -s "$STARTUP_CFG" ]; then

854:     # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)
855:     {
856:         printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\n\r\n' \

865:             # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets

875:                     detail="$(printf '%s' "$result" | sed -n 's/.*"detail":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"

I'll go P4, since it's hardening of a new test, and uncertainty remains.

2. **P4 — 10-second dedup window can swallow a second genuine reboot** (`chr-launch.sh:786-788`). The comment justifies it as collapsing the double RESET of one reboot ("milliseconds apart"), but the window is 10s, so two reboots within 10s of each other result in only one post-reboot NIC check. Impact: minor; if a NIC is rejected on the second boot only, the node stays healthy with a missing data NIC until the next reboot. Suggest narrowing the window (e.g., 2s) or acknowledging with a `ponytail:` comment. Actually — is 2s safe? The two resets of one reboot are "milliseconds apart" per the comment. A second genuine reboot within 2s of the first is also unlikely... but even a 2s window could swallow a fast double reboot. The simplest correction: keep the window but note it, or make it smaller. I'll suggest narrowing to about 2s or a ponytail comment. P4.

3. **P4 — Watcher leaves the node healthy when RouterOS never answers after a reboot** (`chr-launch.sh:765-769`). `after_reboot` waits BOOT_WAIT for REST; on timeout it logs "data NICs not checked" and returns, keeping the ready marker, so the healthcheck keeps reporting `healthy` for a router that is down after a self-reboot. This matches the documented design ("The node stays ready during the reboot… it loses the ready marker only when a NIC is still missing afterwards" — lines 752-753), and is not a regression over base (base had no post-reboot monitoring at all). But since the PR's whole point is post-reboot reliability signaling, a hung RouterOS could cheaply be detected here by also removing the ready marker after the REST deadline. Correction: either `rm -f "$READY_FILE"` in the timeout branch (making the node unhealthy, consistent with the launcher's other FAILED paths) or document the choice. Hmm — careful: removing the marker when RouterOS merely takes longer than BOOT_WAIT to answer would make a slow-but-alive router unhealthy; BOOT_WAIT=300s default is generous. Also note: if RouterOS never comes back, qemu keeps running and nothing else recovers it, so unhealthy is arguably more truthful. I'll present it as P4 with that reasoning.

## Code Review: Re-check data NICs after a RouterOS self-reboot (`mikrotik_chr`)

### Summary

The PR adds a second QMP monitor (`QMP_EVENT_PORT=5002`) and a background watcher in `chr-launch.sh` that re-runs the data-NIC re-plug check after a guest-initiated reboot (`/system reboot`), while the container keeps running. The boot-time check is refactored verbatim into `check_data_nics()`, the test suite gains an end-to-end reboot case, and the docs and script header are updated consistently.

I traced the full flow: the refactor is faithful to the base logic (base lines 503–534 → head `check_data_nics` + caller), both boot paths (first boot at line 892, restart at line 804) call `watch_reboots` only after `ready` and `mgmt_attach`, and QEMU accepts multiple `-qmp` monitors with per-monitor event delivery — so the SeaBIOS/edk2 RESETs that fire before the watcher connects cause no spurious checks. The QMP event format (`"event": "RESET"`, epoch-second `timestamp.seconds`) matches the `case` pattern and the `sed` extraction. `nc` is already used elsewhere in the script, so the watcher introduces no new binary dependency, and the port stays bound to `127.0.0.1` inside the container. The CI workflow `mikrotik_chr-tests.yml` already selects `02*.robot`, so the new test runs automatically. No blocking defects found; three small hardening opportunities below.

| Priority | Count | Summary |
|----------|-------|---------|
| P0 | 0 | — |
| P1 | 0 | — |
| P2 | 0 | — |
| P3 | 0 | — |
| P4 | 3 | Test can pass without the reboot happening; 10 s dedup window can swallow a second reboot; node stays healthy if RouterOS never answers after a reboot |

### Findings

####1. P4 — The reboot test never asserts that the reboot (or the watcher) actually ran**Location:** [`tests/16-mikrotik-chr/02-chr-high-ports.robot` L51–L64](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/tests/16-mikrotik-chr/02-chr-high-ports.robot#L51-L64)

**Problem:** The new test issues `SSHLibrary.Start Command /system reboot`, then asserts that ether64 still forwards traffic and that the node is healthy. Nothing in the test verifies that the reboot — and therefore the new `watch_reboots` path — actually occurred. RouterOS's `/system reboot` normally asks `Reboot, yes? [y/N]:`, and over the non-interactive SSH exec channel that `Start Command` uses, the confirmation input may never arrive, in which case the reboot is aborted and the pre-reboot state trivially satisfies every assertion. The same vacuous pass occurs if the command fails for any other reason.

**Trigger:** The reboot command fails, is aborted at the confirmation prompt, or is simply slower than expected — the test still reports green while the feature path is never exercised.

**Impact:** CI would certify the new post-reboot reliability behavior without ever exercising it, giving false confidence in exactly the scenario this PR targets. (I could not verify RouterOS's prompt behavior over an exec channel without running the lab; source-only review.)

**Correction:** Make the pass conditional on evidence that the reboot happened and was observed. The launcher already logs the line `RouterOS rebooted: checking the data NICs again` (`chr-launch.sh:762`), so the cheapest check is an assertion that `docker logs clab-${lab-name}-r1` contains it after the wait; alternatively assert that RouterOS uptime reset via `/system resource print`.

#### 2. P4 — The 10-second RESET dedup window can swallow a second genuine reboot
**Location:** [`nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh` L781–L791](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh#L781-L791)

**Problem:** `watch_reboots` deduplicates RESET events with `[ "${_ts:-0}" -gt $((_last + 10)) ]`. The comment justifies the window as collapsing the two RESETs of a single reboot, which the comment itself says are milliseconds apart — but the implemented window is 10 seconds, which also collapses two *separate* reboots issued within 10 seconds of each other. The second reboot then gets no post-reboot NIC check.

**Trigger:** An admin (or automation) re-issues `/system reboot` within 10 seconds of a previous one — for example, re-running a failed step in a lab script.

**Impact:** Low but real: if a data NIC is rejected only on the second boot, the node keeps reporting `healthy` with a missing data NIC until the next reboot, defeating the feature's purpose for that case.

**Correction:** Narrow the window to something clearly larger than the millisecond double-reset but smaller than a human re-issuing a reboot (e.g., 2 s), or keep the current value and add a `ponytail:` comment acknowledging that a reboot within 10 s of the previous one goes unchecked. Either is a one-line change.

#### 3. P4 — A RouterOS that never answers after a reboot keeps the node `healthy`
**Location:** [`nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh` L761–L780](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/5e58d57c018a01ed6ebd755f5faa4acd948a9a2d/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh#L761-L780)

**Problem:** In `after_reboot`, if REST does not answer within `$BOOT_WAIT`, the watcher logs `RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s after the reboot: data NICs not checked` and returns, leaving `READY_FILE` in place. The healthcheck therefore keeps reporting `healthy` for a router that is down after a self-reboot. This matches the documented design in the section comment ("the node stays ready during the reboot … it loses the ready marker only when a NIC is still missing afterwards") and is not a regression — the base script had no post-reboot monitoring at all — but the PR introduces the machinery that could cheaply close this gap, since the watcher is already waiting on REST.

**Trigger:** RouterOS hangs or dies during a guest-initiated reboot and never answers REST again.

**Impact:** The node is dead but reported `healthy` indefinitely, so `wait-for` stages and users relying on the default healthcheck trust a non-functioning router.

**Correction:** Either remove `READY_FILE` in the timeout branch of `after_reboot` (consistent with the launcher's other FAILED paths, which withhold the marker; `$BOOT_WAIT` defaults to 300 s, so a merely slow router is unlikely to be misreported), or leave the behavior and document the deliberate limitation in the section comment and the docs paragraph.

### Coverage notes

- Source-only review: I inspected the head and base trees of all three changed paths and their surroundings; I did not execute tests, the launcher, or RouterOS.
- Verified the `check_data_nics` refactor is behavior-preserving against base lines 503–534 (stabilization loop, re-plug rounds, `$miss` semantics, and the failure path's `wait`/`exit 0` all match).
- Verified both boot paths (first boot line 892, restart line 804) run the boot-time check before the watcher starts, and that `watch_reboots` starts after `ready`/`mgmt_attach`, so `after_reboot` has credentials and the REST channel available.
- Verified QMP assumptions from the script's own precedent: `qmp()` already drives the first monitor over busybox `nc`; QMP delivers events only to connected clients (no spurious boot-time checks); the event JSON matches the `case` pattern including the space after the colon.
- Verified CI wiring: `.github/workflows/mikrotik_chr-tests.yml` selects `01*.robot` and `02*.robot`, so the new test runs without workflow changes; `Login via SSH with username and password` exists in `tests/ssh.robot`; `TestLauncherShellSyntax` covers shell syntax of the whole embedded script.
- Docs and the launcher header log-line list were updated consistently; no stale references to "never becomes healthy" remain in the touched doc. No schema relevance: the changes are internal to the launcher script and `clab.schema.json` is untouched and unaffected.
- Unresolved uncertainty: RouterOS's `/system reboot` confirmation behavior over a non-interactive SSH exec channel (see finding 1); I could not verify it from the repository.
- The re-plug gating on `PCI_BRIDGES = 1` (arm64 never re-plugs) is pre-existing behavior preserved by the refactor, not changed by this PR.
